Answer:

## What Happens When Unrelated Text Appears in the Box

When using the **"Begin page group when text in selected area changes"** trigger type, if other unrelated text appears inside the box you drew on the page, **unwanted page groups will be identified (created)**.

This is explicitly stated as an important warning:

> "If other text appears in the box, unwanted page groups are identified."
> [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Why This Happens

The trigger works by monitoring **any text change** within the drawn box. Since the system evaluates all text found within that area, any unrelated text that appears there will be treated as a change, incorrectly triggering the start of a new page group. [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]

---

### How to Avoid This Problem

To prevent unwanted page groups from being created, follow this important guideline:

> **"When you draw the box for this type of page group, make sure that the location of the box on every page encompasses only the text to evaluate or white space (no text)."**
> [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]

Additionally, note that:
- Pages where the box location contains **white space (no text)** will **not** start a new page group. [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]
- This same requirement is reinforced in the product overview: *"The location of the box on every page must encompass only the text to evaluate or white space (no text)."* [pdfw_c_plugin_pagegroupdef.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommended Troubleshooting Steps

If you are already seeing incorrect page groups, you can:

1. Click **Ricoh ⇒ View Page Group Navigator** to inspect the page groups and identify the problem. [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]
2. **Redraw the box**, change the text criteria, or both to correct the issue. [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]
3. Edit the page group definition by double-clicking the box or using the Page Group Navigator. [pdfw_t_plugin_addpagegroups.pdf, Page 2]

Indexed CMRs provide rules about how to render indexed colors. Indexed CMRs apply to indexed colors that are specified by using the highlight color space. They do not apply to indexed colors found within PostScript or other non-IPDS data objects. For Indexed CMRs, both instruction and audit processing modes are valid. ## Indexed CMRs and Audit Processing Mode

When working with Indexed CMRs in AFP color management, **audit processing mode is technically valid but is effectively skipped in practice**.

Here is a precise breakdown:

### What the documentation states:

1. **Both processing modes are recognized as valid** for Indexed CMRs — meaning the system acknowledges that an Indexed CMR *can* be tagged with either instruction or audit processing mode. [cac_CMRIndexed.pdf, Page 1]

2. **However, only Indexed CMRs with an instruction processing mode are actually used.** Those with an audit processing mode are **ignored** entirely by the system. [cac_CMRIndexed.pdf, Page 1]

### Why this matters:

- Audit processing mode is generally used to describe input data that has already been processed — similar to ICC input profiles — and is primarily associated with **color conversion CMRs**. [cac_CMRModeAudit.pdf, Page 1]
- Indexed CMRs serve a different purpose: they map **indexed colors** (specified via the highlight color space) to presentation device colors or colorant combinations. [cac_CMRIndexed.pdf, Page 1]
- This functional difference explains why audit mode has no applicable role for Indexed CMRs.

### Summary Table:

| Processing Mode | Valid for Indexed CMR? | Actually Applied? |
|---|---|---|
| Instruction | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| Audit | ✅ Technically valid | ❌ Ignored |

> **Bottom line:** If you assign an audit processing mode to an Indexed CMR, the system will **not apply it** — it will be silently ignored. Always use **instruction processing mode** for Indexed CMRs. [cac_CMRIndexed.pdf, Page 1]

## Placement of the CombineAFPWithForm Step in a Document-Based AFP Workflow

For a workflow that processes **AFP jobs containing documents**, the placement is clearly specified:

---

### ✅ Recommended Position

Place the **CombineAFPWithForm** step:

- **After** the `BuildAFPFromDocuments` step
- **Before** the `EnableRepositioning` step

> *"To modify a workflow that processes AFP jobs that contain documents, you could put a CombineAFPWithForm step after the BuildAFPFromDocuments step and before the EnableRepositioning step."*
> [ppfrsample_c_ModifyAFPwfForForms.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 📋 Additional Placement Considerations

There is also a related rule to keep in mind:

- If your workflow contains an **afpnorm command** in a step based on the `RunExternalProgram` step template, place the `CombineAFPWithForm` step **after** that `RunExternalProgram` step. [ppfrsample_c_ModifyAFPwfForForms.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚙️ After Placing the Step — Key Property Settings

Once placed, configure the step properties:

1. **Combined AFP file property**: Use the **default value** unless you have special processing requirements. Specifying another value will prevent the combined AFP file from becoming the current print file used by subsequent steps. [ppfrsample_c_ModifyAFPwfForForms.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Tray mapping file property**: If you defined a tray mapping file, set this to the **full path and name** of the file. [ppfrsample_c_ModifyAFPwfForForms.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Important Notes

- The `CombineAFPWithForm` step template is only available when the **Preprinted Forms Replacement**, **PDF Document Support**, and **AFP Support** features are all installed. [ppfrsample_c_ModifyAFPwfForForms.pdf, Page 1]

## Problem with Placing StoreInRepository After ReversePDFPageOrder

Placing a **StoreInRepository** step after a **ReversePDFPageOrder** step causes a **document search reliability problem** in the repository viewer. Here is a detailed explanation:

---

### What Goes Wrong

When a step like **ReversePDFPageOrder** runs, it rearranges the order of pages in the job **at the job level only** — it is not aware of the documents inside the job. [rep_c_PlanForRetention.pdf, Page 2]

The critical issue is this: **document properties remain associated with their original page locations**, even though the actual content of those pages has changed due to the reordering. [rep_c_PlanForRetention.pdf, Page 2]

As a result:
- When you open the job in the viewer and **search using document properties**, the search returns **incorrect or unreliable results**, because the document properties no longer match the actual page content. [rep_c_PlanForRetention.pdf, Page 2]
- Specifically, **searching for a document in a job produces unreliable results**. [rep_c_PlanForRetention.pdf, Page 2]

---

# Configuring Multiple PrintJobs Steps with Conditional Printer Assignment

## Key Principle: Requested Printer on PrintJobs Steps

When you have more than one **PrintJobs** step in a workflow with conditional rules for printer assignment, you should **leave the Requested printer property on each PrintJobs step set to "Any printer"**. [aiw_print_job.pdf, Page 1]

This is necessary because two different PrintJobs steps can only have **one** Requested printer property value — changing it on one step changes it on all others. [aiw_c_hintssteptemplates.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Step-by-Step Configuration

### Step 1 — Set Up the PrintJobs Steps
- Right-click each **PrintJobs** step → **Properties** → **Scheduling** tab.
- Set the **Requested printer** property to **"Any printer"** on every PrintJobs step in the workflow. [aiw_print_job.pdf, Page 1]

### Step 2 — Add an AssignJobValues Step on Each Branch
- Place a step based on the **AssignJobValues** step template **before each PrintJobs step** on every conditional branch. [aiw_c_hintssteptemplates.pdf, Page 1]
- Use the **AssignJobValues** step on each branch to set the **Requested printer** value appropriate for that branch. [aiw_print_job.pdf, Page 1]
- The value set in each **AssignJobValues** step **overrides** the Requested printer property value in the PrintJobs steps. [aiw_c_hintssteptemplates.pdf, Page 1]

### Step 3 — Configure Conditional Rules on Connectors
- Right-click each **connector** between steps and select **Properties** to define conditional processing rules. [aiw_c_addconnectorrule.pdf, Page 1]
- Ensure the rules on connectors exiting the same step are **mutually exclusive**, and that all possible jobs are covered. [aiw_c_addconnectorrule.pdf, Page 1]
- Set the **Order of execution** property on each connector to control the priority in which rules are evaluated. [aiw_c_addconnectorrule.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Practical Example

Here is a concrete example with three branches based on customer name and duplex settings:

| Branch | Connector Rule | AssignJobValues Sets |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | (Customer A or B) AND Duplex = Yes | Requested printer → high quality duplex printer |
| 2 | (Customer C or D) AND Duplex = Yes | Requested printer → standard quality duplex printer |
| 3 | Duplex = No | Requested printer → simplex printer |

[aiw_c_addconnectorrule.pdf, Page 3]

---

## Summary

| Configuration Point | Setting |
|---|---|
| Requested printer on PrintJobs step | **Any printer** |
| Step to set actual printer per branch | **AssignJobValues** |
| Where AssignJobValues is placed | **Before each PrintJobs step, on each branch** |

According to the documentation, before you can send PDF and PostScript files to an InfoPrint 5000 hot folder using RICOH ProcessDirector on Linux, you must do the following three things:

You must define a workflow that includes a **CopyToFolder** step in order to submit print jobs to the hot folder. [ip5khflinux.pdf, Page 1]

## Setting Up a Hot Folder Input Device for Transform Features with AFP Download Plus

When jobs are coming in via **AFP Download Plus**, you should copy a specific existing device template rather than the default transform hot folder device.

### Which Device Template to Copy

Instead of copying the standard `HotFolderTransform` input device, you must copy the **`DownloadAFP` input device** [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].

### Full Step-by-Step Setup Instructions

1. Click the **Administration** tab [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
2. In the left pane, click **Devices ⇒ Input Devices** [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
3. **Right-click the `DownloadAFP` input device** and select **Copy** (since your jobs are submitted using AFP Download Plus) [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
4. Type a **name** and a **description** for the new input device [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
5. On the **General** tab, find the **Child workflow** property and select the workflow you created to send jobs to be transformed [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
6. Click the **Batching** tab [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
7. Check the **Data patterns** property to ensure RICOH ProcessDirector can correctly identify the files to send for transformation (e.g., set to `.*PDF$` for PDF files with `.PDF` extensions) [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
8. Click **OK** [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].
9. To activate the new input device, right-click it and select **Enable and Connect** [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].

### ⚠️ Important Prerequisite

> You **must have the AFP Support feature installed** in order to use the RICOH Transform features to receive jobs from AFP Download Plus [aiwctransid.pdf, Page 1].

## Headers File for IdentifyPDFDocuments: Only Include What You Need

No, you do **not** need to include every column from your auxiliary data file. You only need to include the columns you actually plan to use in the workflow.

Here is how it works:

---

### How the Headers File Works

The headers file lists only the **database names of the document properties whose values you want to add to the Document Properties File (DPF)**. Each database property name is placed on a separate line. [pdfw_c_SetInputForPDFWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Example

Answer:

## When to Set 'Stop When No Matching Elements' to **No**

You should set **'Stop when no matching elements'** to **No** when **some XML input files may have no elements that match the XPath expression**, and you want the job to **continue to the next step in the workflow** rather than go into error when no matching elements are found. [aiw_c_xml_DefineWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Detailed Guidance

| Setting | When to Use |
|--------|-------------|
| **Yes** | Every XML input file is guaranteed to have one or more matching elements. You want the job to go into **error** if no match is found. [aiw_c_xml_DefineWorkflow.pdf, Page 1] |
| **No** | Some XML input files may legitimately have **no matching elements**. You want the job to **continue** to the next step without error. [aiw_c_xml_DefineWorkflow.pdf, Page 1] |

---

### Practical Example

A clear real-world example of when to use **No** is:

> A `CreateJobsFromXML` step creates an XML job for each **print item** in an order. However, orders can contain **print items, promotional items, or both**. Since some orders may have no print items at all, you want the job to **continue to the next step** in the workflow when no matching print item elements are found — rather than failing with an error. [aiw_c_xml_DefineWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

This scenario is also illustrated in the multi-step workflow example, where separate `CreateJobsFromXML` steps handle print items (`/order/item/printfile/ancestor::item`) and promotional items (`/order/item/stock/ancestor::item`) independently, since an order may contain one type but not the other. [aiw_o_xml_scen_orders.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

Set **'Stop when no matching elements'** to **No** whenever the **absence of matching XML elements is a valid, expected condition** for some input files, and the workflow should proceed normally in that case.

## Why You Get an Error When Copying Certain Step Templates

When you right-click a step template and select **Copy**, you may receive an error message instead of being able to copy it. This is expected behaviour for certain built-in step templates that have a **copy restriction** applied to them.

---

### Explanation

RICOH ProcessDirector provides step templates that you can normally copy to create custom step templates. However, **some step templates cannot be copied by design**. If you attempt to copy one of these restricted templates, the system will display an error message rather than opening the copy dialog. [aiw00c11.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Which Templates Have This Limitation?

The documentation specifically identifies the following step templates as **non-copyable**:

- **PrintJobs**
- **RemoveJobs**

> *"Some step templates, such as PrintJobs and RemoveJobs, cannot be copied. You see an error message if you try to copy them."* [aiw00c11.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What You Should Do Instead

If you need a custom step template, use one of the **copyable** step templates as your starting point. For example:

- To create a custom **manual step**, copy the **ManualStepWithAutoStart** step template. [aiw00c11.pdf, Page 1]
- To create a custom **external step using command line or control files**, copy the **RunExternalProgram** step template. [aiwcstextstepnothot.pdf, Page 1]
- To create a custom **external step using hot folders**, copy the **RunHotFolderApplication** step template. [aiwcstextstephot.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Step Template | Can Be Copied? |
|---|---|
| ManualStepWithAutoStart | ✅ Yes |
| RunExternalProgram | ✅ Yes |
| RunHotFolderApplication | ✅ Yes |
| **PrintJobs** | ❌ No — error message shown |
| **RemoveJobs** | ❌ No — error message shown |

## Wait Step: Calculating End Times and Advancing the Job

Based on the documentation, here is a precise explanation of how the Wait step handles this exact scenario:

---

### The Scenario

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Wait until** | 12:00 PM |
| **Time zone** | Eastern Standard Time (EST) |
| **Wait for** | 3 hours |
| **Job arrival time** | 10:00 AM EST |

---

### Step 1: Calculating the Two Possible End Times

When both **Wait until** and **Wait for** are configured, the step calculates an end time for **each option independently** [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]:

1. **Wait until end time** → **12:00 PM EST**
   (the fixed time specified in the configuration) [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Wait for end time** → **1:00 PM EST**
   (job arrived at 10:00 AM EST + 3 hours = 1:00 PM EST) [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: How 'Complete Step After' Determines When the Job Advances

The **Complete step after** setting controls which of the two calculated end times triggers the job to move to the next step [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]:

- **If set to "First occurs"** → The job advances at **12:00 PM EST**, because that is the earlier of the two end times. [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]

- **If set to "Last occurs"** → The job advances at **1:00 PM EST**, because that is the later of the two end times. [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 3: Verifying the Calculated Wait End Time

To confirm when the waiting period for a specific job will end, you can check the **Wait step ends** property, found on the **Wait tab** of the job property notebook. [aiw_c_addwaitstep.pdf, Page 1]

If a workflow or an authorized user changes the Adjusted arrival time property for a job, RICOH ProcessDirector recalculates the checkpoints for the job. ## How Phase Intervals Are Calculated When No Adjustment Method Is Set

When no adjustment method is set on a service policy, **all phase intervals start from the same checkpoint start time** — they do **not** stack sequentially on top of each other.

---

### Key Principle

> *"The interval for each phase starts from the checkpoint start time, which is the same time for all intervals."*
> [slapolicyintervals.pdf, Page 1]

This means each interval **includes** the time needed to complete all previous phases, rather than beginning where the previous phase ended. [slapolicyintervals.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Specific Behavior When Adjustment Method = None

When the adjustment method is **None**:

- The **checkpoint start time = the adjusted arrival time** [slapolicyintervals.pdf, Page 1]
- If the adjusted arrival time has not been reset, it equals the **job arrival time** [slapolicyintervals.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Concrete Example

The documentation provides this illustrative example (jobs must be printed 4 hours after arrival):

| Phase | Interval | Deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Receive | 20 minutes | Job arrival + 20 min |
| Prepare | 2 hours | Job arrival + 2 hours |
| Print | 4 hours | Job arrival + 4 hours |

All three intervals **start from the same point** (job arrival time), not from the end of the preceding phase. [slapolicyintervals.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

The intervals **do not stack** — they all originate from the same checkpoint start time. Each successive interval is simply **longer**, naturally encompassing the time required for all prior phases. [slapolicyintervals.pdf, Page 1]

## Range Parameter in AFP Pipeline Filters: Explanation of '0:7' and 'e'

### Format of the Range Parameter

The Range parameter follows the format **"first:last"**, where the first value starts at zero (0). [ave_Pipeline_filters.pdf, Page 2]

---

### What does '0:7' mean?

**`0:7` means the first eight objects.**

This is because counting starts at zero (0), so the range from position 0 to position 7 covers 8 elements in total (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7). [ave_Pipeline_filters.pdf, Page 2]

---

### What does the letter 'e' represent?

The letter **'e' stands for "end"** — it represents the last element in the file.

For example:
- **`0:e`** means **from the beginning to the end of the file** (i.e., all elements). [ave_Pipeline_filters.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Summary Table

| Range Value | Meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| `0:7` | The first eight objects (positions 0 through 7) |
| `0:e` | From the beginning to the end of the file |

This Range parameter is available as an **optional parameter** in several filters, including **Cut AFP Objects**, **Cut AFP Structured Fields**, and **Remove Page Groups**. [ave_Pipeline_filters.pdf, Page 2]

## Function of `downloadOverrides.xslt` in the MarcomCentral Ticket Workflow

### What the file does

The `downloadOverrides.xslt` file is an XSLT style sheet used by the **ApplyXSLTransform2** step within the MarcomDownloadPrintFile step chain. It converts a specific XML element from the MarcomCentral job ticket response into a RICOH ProcessDirector job property. Specifically, it **retrieves the URL of the print file** from the SOAP response and copies that URL into a job property so that a subsequent step can use it to download the print file. [mcc_c_DefineTicketWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

The file is located at the following path on the server:
`/aiw/aiw1/testfiles/Marcom` [mcc_c_RunSOAPmccWF.pdf, Page 1]

---

### XML Element-to-Job Property Mapping

The `downloadOverrides.xslt` file maps the following XML element to a RICOH ProcessDirector job property:

| XML Element | Database Name of Job Property | UI Name of Job Property |
|---|---|---|
| `JobTicket/FinalOutputFileURL/URL` | `Job.Info.Attr3` | **Custom 3** |

[mcc_c_RunSOAPmccWF.pdf, Page 2]

---

### How the value is used downstream

After the ApplyXSLTransform2 step applies the transformation, it **puts the value into an overrides file** and overwrites the overrides file in the spool directory for the job. [mcc_c_RunSOAPmccWF.pdf, Page 2]

The **DownloadFile** step then uses the populated `Custom 3` property via the symbol `${Job.Info.Attr3}` as the value for its **URL for download file** property to retrieve the actual print file. [mcc_c_RunSOAPmccWF.pdf, Page 3]

---

### Customization Note

You can use the `downloadOverrides.xslt` file as-is. However, if you need to retrieve **additional information** from MarcomCentral beyond the print file URL, you can create a new XSLT file and update the **XSLT file** property on the ApplyXSLTransform2 step accordingly. [mcc_c_DefineTicketWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

External steps can access files in the spool directory for the job. When RICOH ProcessDirector creates a job from an input file, it creates a unique spool directory. The spool directory contains a copy of the input file and other files that provide information about the job. External steps can call programs that update existing files in the spool directory and write new files to the directory. The default spool directory for a job is /aiw/aiw1/spool/default/JobNumber (JobNumber is the spool ID that RICOH ProcessDirector assigns to the job). On an application server, the spool directory is mounted on the drive that you chose when you installed the application server. The default is Z:\aiw1\spool\default\JobNumber. You can also create additional spool directories. These spool directories have names in this format: /aiw/aiw1/spool/SpoolName/JobNumber (SpoolName is the subdirectory name that the authorized user defined). The programs that the external steps call can also create child jobs. The spool directory contains a /aiw/aiw1/spool/default/JobNumber/children subdirectory or a /aiw/aiw1/spool/SpoolName/JobNumber/children directory that external program can use to write its child jobs and their associated files. ## Steps to Test External Step Processing in RICOH ProcessDirector

After you set up step templates for external steps and add steps to workflows, you should configure the method of workflow assignment and run test jobs **before** running any production jobs. [aiwctestextstep.pdf, Page 1]

Follow these steps:

---

### Step 1: Configure the Input Device
Determine how you want to assign the workflow that contains the external step to jobs, and configure the input device accordingly. [aiwctestextstep.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: Submit a Test Job
Submit a job to the input device, and view the log for the job after processing completes. [aiwctestextstep.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 3: Review Results and Troubleshoot if Necessary
If **either** of the following situations occurs, use the messages in the log to identify and correct the problem: [aiwctestextstep.pdf, Page 1]

- The job did **not** complete its processing and is in an **error state**, **OR**
- Processing was successful but the **results were not as expected**.

---

### Additional Context
Before reaching the testing phase, ensure you have completed the preceding configuration tasks in order: [aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

1. **Setting up external programs** – Install and verify the external program operates correctly as a standalone program. [aiw_sdk_extprog.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Setting up step templates for external steps** – Create a step template containing the command that calls the external program, and tune it to run on the appropriate Linux or Windows system. [aiwcstextstep.pdf, Page 1]
3. **Setting up workflows for external steps** – Add a step based on the step template to a workflow and assign the workflow to an input device. [aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

Only after completing all of the above should you proceed with the testing steps outlined above. [aiwctestextstep.pdf, Page 1]

The step template in AFP Support that lets you update document properties based on other document and job property values is the **SetDocPropsFromConditions** step template.

# Web Services Input Devices and Batch Job Submission in RICOH ProcessDirector

## Short Answer

Web services input devices in RICOH ProcessDirector are **not** used to submit batch jobs. Their purpose is to **retrieve/pull data from external applications**, not to submit jobs. However, web services **can** be used to submit jobs through a different mechanism — the REST web service utility.

---

## Detailed Explanation

### What Web Services Input Devices Actually Do

Web services input devices (REST and SOAP) are designed to **call external web services to retrieve data**, not to submit batch jobs:

- **REST web service input devices** call a REST web service to retrieve XML or JSON files from an application and create jobs from that retrieved content. [aiw00o4.pdf, Page 1]
- **SOAP web service input devices** call a SOAP web service to retrieve XML files from an application and create jobs from the retrieved content. [aiw00o4.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ Both device types are only available if the **Web Services Enablement feature** is installed. [aiw00o4.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Submitting Jobs via Web Services (The Correct Approach)

If you want to **submit** jobs using web services, RICOH ProcessDirector provides a **REST web service utility** (`submitFile`). Here is how it works:

1. **Decide how RICOH ProcessDirector receives the file:**
   - Submit directly to a **workflow** when there is only one input file per job or you do not need batching functions.
   - Submit to a **hot folder** when you want to use the **batching functions** in RICOH ProcessDirector. [aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Note:** You can only submit **one file at a time** with the web service. If a job has multiple input files (job tickets, list files, etc.), you must invoke the web service for each file. [aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Use the REST API documentation** (`http://hostname:15080/restapi/`) and locate:
   `POST /util/submitFile/{objectType}/{name}` [aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1]

4. **Configure your application** with the appropriate Curl command or Request URL. [aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1]

5. **Verify** the submission by checking that files appear in the hot folder directory, or that a job is created in the workflow. [aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Mechanism | Purpose | Supports Batching? |
|---|---|---|
| REST/SOAP web service **input devices** | Pull/retrieve data from external apps | No (retrieval only) |
| REST `submitFile` utility → **Hot folder** | Submit jobs via web service | ✅ Yes |
| REST `submitFile` utility → **Workflow** | Submit jobs via web service | ❌ No |

[aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1] [aiw00o4.pdf, Page 1]

---

**In conclusion:** To submit batch jobs using web services, you should use the **REST `submitFile` utility directed at a hot folder input device**, not the web services input devices themselves. [aiw_c_PrepToSumbitWebservice.pdf, Page 1]

## Importazione WSDL in ProcessDirector: Nomi degli Oggetti e Posizione del File

### Cosa succede ai nomi degli oggetti SOAP Request

Quando si imposta un prefisso come **'DigitalStore'** durante l'importazione di un file WSDL, RICOH ProcessDirector **antepone questo valore e un trattino** al nome di ciascun oggetto SOAP request che crea [ws-step_c_ImportWSDL.pdf, Page 1].

**Esempio pratico:**
Se il file WSDL contiene due SOAP request:
- `GetOrdersByDate`
- `GetOrdersByOrderNumber`

Dopo l'importazione con il prefisso `DigitalStore`, i nomi dei due oggetti SOAP request diventeranno:
- **`DigitalStore-GetOrdersByDate`**
- **`DigitalStore-GetOrdersByOrderNumber`**

[ws-step_c_ImportWSDL.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Dove viene salvato il file WSDL su Linux

Il sistema utilizza il **valore del prefisso WSDL** come nome del file salvato. L'estensione del file sarà nel formato `wsdl-number`, dove *number* è un **numero di 13 cifre** [ws-step_c_ImportWSDL.pdf, Page 1].

**Esempio del nome file risultante:**
```
DigitalStore.wsdl-1234567890123
```

**Percorso di archiviazione su Linux:**
```
/aiw/aiw1/wsdl
```

[ws-step_c_ImportWSDL.pdf, Page 1]

## Setting Up JDF Job Ticket Processing in RICOH ProcessDirector

### Required Step Template in the Workflow

When configuring a workflow to handle JDF job ticket processing, the workflow **must contain a step based on the `SetJobPropsFromTextFile` step template**. This is a mandatory requirement before jobs with JDF job tickets can be processed correctly. [aiw00cjdf.pdf, Page 1]

## Setting Up a Passthrough Printer to Print Banner Pages Separately (Not Merged)

When the **Merge banner pages into PDF print file** property is set to **No**, the **Printer command** property must be updated to include **multiple `lpr` commands** — one for the job and one for each type of banner page that is enabled. [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What the Printer Command Must Include

The command must contain:
- **One `lpr` command** for each enabled banner page type (header and/or trailer)
- **One `lpr` command** for the actual PDF job itself [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Required Order of `lpr` Commands

The commands must be entered **in the order that the pages should print**. [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

For a job that has **both a header page and a trailer page**, the correct order is:

1. **Header page** (first)
2. **PDF job** (second)
3. **Trailer page** (third)

The example command provided is:

```bash
lpr -P printerName ${getFileName(header,pdf,read)} && \
lpr -P printerName ${getCurrentFile(pdf)} && \
lpr -P printerName ${getFileName(trailer,pdf,read)}
```
[aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Important Notes

- The printer device **must support the PDF data stream** in order to print these banner pages. [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]
- The **Header copies** and **Trailer copies** job properties must each be set to **1 or greater**; if set to 0, the banner pages will not print — and if they are requested in the printer command but set to 0, **the job will not print correctly**. [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]
- When **Merge** is set to **No**, be aware that **another job sent to the printer at the same time might print between the job and its banner pages**. [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

## AFP Editor: Hidden Areas and Original Data

No, the original data is **not permanently removed** from the AFP file when AFP Editor hides an area.

AFP Editor creates a hidden area by generating an AFP graphics object that contains no data and that prints in the color of the medium — effectively painting over the existing content. However, the underlying data remains intact in the file. [hiddenareas_overview.pdf, Page 1]

As the documentation explicitly states:

> *"Although you cannot use an AFP viewer to see the existing data in the hidden area, the data still exists in the AFP file."* [hiddenareas_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What "hiding" actually does:

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Visual effect** | The area is invisible to AFP viewers and does not print [hiddenareas_overview.pdf, Page 1] |
| **Mechanism** | An AFP graphics object with no data, printed in the medium's color, is overlaid on the area [hiddenareas_overview.pdf, Page 1] |
| **Original data** | **Still exists** in the AFP file — it is only covered, not deleted [hiddenareas_overview.pdf, Page 1] |

---

### If you want to reveal the data again:

You can delete the hidden area definition, which will restore visibility of the original data. When a hidden area is deleted from the definitions list, **"you see any data that the hidden area covered in the AFP file"** reappear. [deletinghiddenareas.pdf, Page 1]

## Role of the PrintForPostalProcess Workflow

### Primary Role

The **PrintForPostalProcess** workflow is responsible for **printing the child jobs** created by the `GroupDocsForPostalProcess` workflow. It ensures that the order of documents within each job is correct for each type of mail it handles. [mail_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Types of Mail Handled

The `PrintForPostalProcess` workflow handles **three types of mail**, all arriving as child jobs from the `GroupDocsForPostalProcess` workflow:

1. **Qualified Mail** – Child jobs that have already been processed by the `ProcessQualifiedDocuments` workflow (which sorts them using postal software) are passed on to `PrintForPostalProcess` for final printing. [mail_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Non-Qualified Mail** – Documents that do not qualify for additional postal processing. These are sorted in **zip code order**, but not using postal software. [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Other Mail** – Documents that fall into neither the Qualified nor Non-Qualified category. These are sorted by **number of sheets**. [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Processing Actions

For all child jobs it receives, the `PrintForPostalProcess` workflow performs the following:

- **Removes the PostNet barcode** from the original job. [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]
- **Adds a 2D Datamatrix barcode** for mail piece tracking, identifying the job number and document number. [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]

This is accomplished using specific control files for each mail type:
- `PostalPDFBuildQualify.ctl` – for Qualified documents (also adds an **Intelligent Mail barcode**). [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]
- `PostalPDFBuildNonQualify.ctl` – for Non-Qualified documents. [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]
- `PostalPDFBuildOther.ctl` – for Other documents. [mail_o_RunningGroupDocsPrintAndProcessWorkflows.pdf, Page 1]

## What Happens When a Job is Submitted via FTP with the Wrong User ID

### What Happens to the Job

If a user submits a job via FTP using a user ID that is **not a member of the RICOH ProcessDirector group**, RICOH ProcessDirector will not have the correct access permissions set on the input file and **cannot process the job**. As a result:

> **The job stays in Error state in the Receive phase until it is deleted and resubmitted correctly.**

[aiw00c30.pdf, Page 1]

### Why This Happens

During installation, RICOH ProcessDirector creates a dedicated group (the default is **aiwgrp1**) and grants the RICOH ProcessDirector system user (default: **aiw1**) authority to that group. Only users whose IDs belong to this RICOH ProcessDirector group have the correct permissions to allow RICOH ProcessDirector to access submitted files. [aiw00c30.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Fix It

There are **two parts** to the fix:

#### 1. Fix the Stuck Job
- **Delete** the job that is currently stuck in Error state in the Receive phase.
- **Resubmit** the job correctly, using a user ID that is a member of the RICOH ProcessDirector group. [aiw00c30.pdf, Page 1]

#### 2. Prevent It from Happening Again
Ensure that the submitting user's ID is added to the RICOH ProcessDirector group on the primary computer. Important notes when doing this:
- Use the RICOH ProcessDirector group name as an **additional group** for the user — **not** as their default group.
- Inform all job submitters that they **must be logged in with a user ID that is a member of the RICOH ProcessDirector group** when submitting jobs via FTP or SCP. [aiw00c30.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| FTP job submitted with correct group member user ID | Job is processed normally |
| FTP job submitted with wrong/non-member user ID | Job stuck in **Error state** in the **Receive phase** |
| Resolution | Delete the job and resubmit with a valid group member user ID |

## Step That Sets Initial Job Property Values

When RICOH ProcessDirector first assigns a workflow to a job, the **SetJobPropsFromTextFile** step is responsible for reading through all the workflow steps and setting initial job property values.

Specifically, when RICOH ProcessDirector assigns a workflow to a job, the **SetJobPropsFromTextFile** step processes **all of the steps in the workflow** and assigns values to job properties set by those steps. [aiw_SetJobDef.Wrkflw.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Service Policies and Schedule-Based Tracking with Estimated Durations

**No** — service policies are **not** used when tracking jobs against a schedule based on estimated durations.

This is explicitly stated in the documentation:

> *"Service policies are not used when tracking to a schedule based on estimated durations or to a deadline set by a SetDeadline step or the Change Deadline action."*
> [slacreatingpolicies.pdf, Page 1] [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]

### Summary of When Service Policies Apply

Service policies are specifically designed to define **job checkpoints** that help track whether jobs are on schedule to meet the performance commitments in a **Service Level Agreement (SLA)**. [slacreatingpolicies.pdf, Page 1]

They are **not** applicable in the following tracking scenarios:
1. **Tracking to a schedule** based on estimated durations [slacreatingpolicies.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Tracking to a deadline** set by a `SetDeadline` step or the **Change Deadline** action [slacreatingpolicies.pdf, Page 1]

### How Schedule-Based Tracking (Estimated Durations) Works Instead

When tracking to a schedule using estimated durations, RICOH ProcessDirector uses the estimated durations set on workflow steps to calculate and display the following properties on the job: [dt_o_featov.pdf, Page 2]

- **Percent complete** — how much of the estimated duration has completed
- **Tracking status** — whether the job is on schedule or behind schedule
- **Predicted completion time** — calculated by adding up estimated durations across the predicted job path

If a job falls behind schedule, a **yellow dot** appears in the Deadlines portlet and in the Schedule risk column in the Jobs table. [dt_o_featov.pdf, Page 2]

## Monitoring Multiple Object Types in a Single ProcessDirector Notification

No, you **cannot** monitor more than one type of object in a single email notification. Each notification object is limited to a single object type.

### Key Limitation

When creating an email notification, the documentation explicitly states:

> *"Select the type of object to be monitored. You can only use **one type of Event type** for each notification."*
> [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]

### What You Can Monitor (Per Notification)

Each individual notification can monitor **one** of the following object types [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]:

- **Input devices**
- **Jobs**
- **Printers**

### Recommended Workaround

To monitor multiple object types (e.g., both jobs and printers), you must **create separate notification objects** — one for each object type. The documentation confirms this approach:

> *"Create one or more notification objects, **one for every type of event** that you want to be notified about."*
> [not_setup_notification.pdf, Page 1]

### Example

| Notification Object | Object Type | Event Example |
|---|---|---|
| Notification A | Printer | Printer enters error state |
| Notification B | Job | Job enters error state |

You can define **any number of notification objects** based on the needs of your shop [not_o_NotifObj.pdf, Page 1], so there is no restriction on how many separate notifications you create.

## RICOH Visual Workbench – Form Definition Selection: Is It Remembered?

**No, your choice will NOT be remembered the next time you open the file.**

According to the documentation, the behavior is explicitly stated:

> *"If you specify a form definition other than the default, it is **not saved in the control file**. Therefore, each time you open the AFP file, you must specify the form definition if you want to see the medium map information."*
> [formdefinition.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What this means in practice:

1. **Each session requires manual re-selection.** If you choose a non-default form definition (either by typing a directory path or using the Browse button), that selection is lost when you close the file. [formdefinition.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Only the inline form definition option persists differently** — you can click **"Use Inline Form Definition"** to override the default, but any custom directory-based form definition you specify is still not saved. [formdefinition.pdf, Page 1]

3. **To re-apply your form definition next time**, you must repeat these steps each session:
   - Open the AFP file in RICOH Visual Workbench.
   - Click **Resources ⇒ Change Form Definition Settings**.
   - Re-enter or re-browse to your desired form definition.
   - Click **OK**. [formdefinition.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Form Definition Type | Saved in Control File? |
|---|---|
| Default form definition | ✅ Yes (default behavior) |
| Inline form definition | Used if selected, but not persisted as a path |
| **Non-default (custom) form definition** | ❌ **No – must re-specify each session** |

# Conditional Workflow: SetDeadline Step Placement and Configuration

## Where to Place the SetDeadline Step

In a conditional workflow with separate paths for PDF, AFP, and PostScript/PCL jobs, you place **a SetDeadline step at the start of each individual path** — one per branch. [dt_o_scen_deadlineconditionwf.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Step-by-Step Configuration

### Step 1: Add the SetDeadline Step to Each Path

1. In the workflow editor, click the side panel in the top right corner of the window. [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]
2. Go to **Steps** and expand the **TRACKING** group. [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]
3. Select the **SetDeadline** step template and drag it into the workflow editor, placing it at the **start of each conditional path**. [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: Configure Each SetDeadline Step

Right-click each SetDeadline step, select **Properties**, then click **Deadline** and configure as follows: [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]

| Path | Deadline Step | Deadline Date Setting | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PDF jobs** | PrintJobs | Relative to property value; Property = Time submitted | **+2 hours** |
| **AFP jobs** | PrintJobs | Relative to property value; Property = Time submitted | **+90 minutes** |
| **PostScript/PCL jobs** | PrintJobs | Relative to property value; Property = Time submitted | **+30 minutes** |

[dt_o_scen_deadlineconditionwf.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Resulting Workflow Structure

The complete workflow follows this structure: [dt_o_scen_deadlineconditionwf.pdf, Page 1]

**Shared steps (all jobs):**
- `SetJobPropsFromTextFile` → `DetectInputDataStream`

**Path for PDF jobs:**
- `SetDeadline` (2 hours) → `Preflight` → `CountPages` → `PrintSetup` → `CreatePageRanges`

**Path for AFP jobs:**
- `SetDeadline` (90 minutes) → `CountPages` → `Accounting` → `PrintSetup` → `CreatePageRanges`

**Path for other jobs (PostScript/PCL):**
- `SetDeadline` (30 minutes) → `PrintSetup`

**Shared steps (all jobs):**
- `PrintJobs` → `RetainCompletedJobs` → `RemoveJobs`

---

## What Happens When a Deadline Is Missed

If a job misses its deadline, RICOH ProcessDirector adds a **red dot** to the **Schedule risk** column for the job in the Jobs table: [dt_o_scen_deadlineconditionwf.pdf, Page 1]

- 🔴 Red dot for **PDF jobs** after **2 hours**
- 🔴 Red dot for **AFP jobs** after **90 minutes**
- 🔴 Red dot for **PostScript/PCL jobs** after **30 minutes**

## RICOH ProcessDirector – Object Log Retention & Audit File Purge Schedule

Here is a clear breakdown of the two retention periods you asked about:

---

### 1. 📋 Object Log Data Retention (Before Moving to Audit Files)

**Object logs keep data for the last 3 days.**

After 3 days, the log information is automatically moved to audit files located in the `/aiw/aiw1/audit/<object type>` directory. [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1]

> **Important exception – Job Logs:** Job logs behave differently. They remain in the system **as long as the job itself exists**. Only when the job is deleted does the log information get moved to the audit files. [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. 🗂️ Audit File Retention (Before Being Purged)

**Audit files remain in the system for 28 days**, after which they are **automatically deleted**. [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Data Type | Retention Period | What Happens After |
|---|---|---|
| Object logs | **3 days** | Moved to audit files in `/aiw/aiw1/audit/` [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1] |
| Job logs | **Until job is deleted** | Moved to audit files upon job deletion [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1] |
| Audit files | **28 days** | Automatically purged [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1] |

---

> 📝 **Additional note:** There is **no size limit** for logs. [aiw00p7.pdf, Page 1]

## Repositioning an AFP Print Job with Multiple Copies: Jumping to a Specific Page

Based on the available documentation, here is a clear answer to your question:

**No, you cannot directly jump to a specific page number in a different copy.** When a job consists of multiple copies, a different method is required.

---

### How It Works for Multi-Copy Jobs

When using the **Jump to** action on an AFP print job with multiple copies:

- **You can only specify a page in the *current* copy.** [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
- **To back up or skip ahead to a page in a *different* copy, you must specify which *side* of the job to jump to** — not a page number. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Process for Repositioning

1. Using the job number shown under the printer icon, find the job in the Jobs table and confirm it is in the **Print phase** and **Printing state**. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
2. In the **Printers Portlet**, select the printer and click **Stop**. For multiple copies, select either **Immediately** or **After the current copy prints**. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
3. In the **Jobs portlet**, select the job that was printing. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
4. Click **Actions ⇒ Jump to**. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
5. On the **Jump to a Location** page:
   - Since the job has multiple copies, **specify which side of the job to jump to** in order to reach a page in a different copy. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
6. Select whether to perform a **non-process runout (NPRO)** action before resuming printing. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
7. Click **OK**. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]
8. In the **Printers Portlet**, click **Start** to resume printing. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Additional Note

If the **Interrupt Message Page** property for the printer is set to **Yes**, the printer will print a message page for the repositioning action, and the restart point might be off by one sheet. To avoid this:
- Set **Interrupt Message Page** to **No**, or
- Use the **Resume printing at page** control instead of the **Back up** or **Skip ahead** controls. [aiw00p4.pdf, Page 1]

## Switching to the Correct Control File in RICOH Visual Workbench

If you accidentally loaded the wrong control file after opening a sample AFP file, here is how to switch to the correct one:

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

**Step 1: Use the File menu to open a different control file**

Click **File ⇒ Open Control File** and select the correct control file. [creatingcontrolfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

**Step 2: Handle the warning message (if it appears)**

If you have already made enhancements to the AFP file during the current session, you will see the following warning message:

> *"Your unsaved changes will be lost if you open a new control file. Do you want to continue?"*

[creatingcontrolfiles.pdf, Page 1]

At this point, you have **two options** depending on whether you want to preserve your work:

---

### ⚠️ Option A — You want to SAVE your work first (recommended to avoid losing changes)

1. Click **No** to cancel opening the new control file.
2. **Save the currently open control file** (via **File ⇒ Save control file as**, entering the full path name, and clicking **Save**).
3. Once saved, go back to **File ⇒ Open Control File** and select the correct control file.

[creatingcontrolfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Option B — You do NOT need to keep the changes made in this session

1. Click **Yes** to proceed.
2. The wrong control file will be replaced by the correct one, but **any unsaved enhancements made in this session will be lost**.

[creatingcontrolfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Reminder

All definitions that apply to a sample AFP file **must be contained within the same control file**. You should always ensure the correct control file is associated with your sample AFP file before making enhancements. [creatingcontrolfiles.pdf, Page 1] [workbenchcontrolfiles.pdf, Page 1]

## Swapping Part of a Text String in Whitespace Manager

Here is a step-by-step guide to replace part of an existing text string — for example, changing **"Page 1 of 10"** to **"Page 1 for John Doe"** — using the Modify Text function in RICOH Visual Workbench Whitespace Manager:

---

### Step 1: Open the Modify Text Window

1. In RICOH Visual Workbench, open a sample AFP file and the control file that contains the white space definitions. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
2. Click **Mode ⇒ Whitespace Manager**. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
3. Click **Tools ⇒ Manage Campaigns**. The Manage Campaigns window appears. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
4. Select a **rule** from the list in the top pane of the window. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
5. Select **text content** from the drop-down list. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
6. Click **Edit** in the Content section. The **Modify Text** window appears. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: Remove the Parts You Want to Replace

On the **Text tab**, in the Text string data section: [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

1. Press and hold the **CTRL key**, then select **"of"** and **"Page Count"** (the two items you want to remove). [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
2. Click **Remove** to delete those selected lines. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 3: Add the Replacement Text and Index Tag

1. Type **`for`** in the **Text field** and click **Add**. *(Remember to include a leading/trailing space if needed to separate words.)* [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
2. From the **Index tag** drop-down list, select the index tag that contains the customer name (e.g., "John Doe"), then click **Add**. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

> The edited text string value will be displayed in the field below the data fields. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 4: Confirm and Preview

1. Click **OK** to save the changes. You will see the edited text. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Optional:** Click **Preview** to view how the updated text is displayed in the defined white space. Close the preview by clicking the **X** in the upper right corner. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 💡 Key Tips

- Always **add blank characters between words** manually if needed, as spacing is not added automatically. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
- You can use **Up** or **Down** buttons to reorder lines in the text string at any time. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]
- Measurement units (inches or millimeters) can be changed via **View ⇒ Units**. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1]

## AFP Banner Page Configuration File Locations on Linux

On a Linux system, AFP banner page configuration files are stored in **two separate directories**:

---

### 1. 📁 Sample Files Directory
**`/aiw/aiw1/samples/banner_pages/`**

This is where RICOH ProcessDirector installs the **sample/default control files**. RICOH ProcessDirector provides twelve control files for various types of AFP banner pages in this location. [aiw00c31.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ **Important Warning:** Updates may **overwrite** files in this directory. You should not make your customizations here. [aiw00bannerbcode.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. 📁 Active/Working Configuration Files Directory
**`/aiw/aiw1/control_files/banner_pages/`**

This is where your **active, customized control files** should be stored (e.g., `header.cfg`). Files in this directory are **not overwritten** by system updates. [aiw00c31.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ✅ Recommended Workflow

1. Copy the desired sample file from `/aiw/aiw1/samples/banner_pages/` to `/aiw/aiw1/control_files/banner_pages/`. [aiw00c31.pdf, Page 1]
2. Make all your edits to the **copied file** in the `control_files` directory. [aiw00bannerbcode.pdf, Page 1]
3. Reference the modified file in the **Header page configuration file**, **Trailer page configuration file**, or **Separator page configuration file** property on the workflow or individual job. [aiw00c31.pdf, Page 1]

---

> 💡 Note: This same two-directory structure also applies to the `banner_page_code_page_mapping.cfg` configuration file used for coded font and code page mappings. [aiw_afpbanners.pdf, Page 1]

## MarcomCloseoutOrder Notification: What It Sends and Alternatives for Invoicing/Settlements

### What the Sample MarcomCloseoutOrder Notification Sends

The sample **MarcomCloseoutOrder** SOAP web service notification is designed to send order completion information to MarcomCentral. Specifically, it simulates a call to the web service at `https://services.printable.com/Trans/1.0/Closeout.asmx`, using the SOAP request **MarcomSample-CloseoutByOrder** [mcc_c_RunSOAPmccWF.pdf, Page 1].

In its core configuration, the **Request URL and Request payload properties** of the notification are set to call the **Order Closeout MarcomCentral web service** and send the **ID of the completed order** [mcc_c_PrepToSendStatus.pdf, Page 1].

When the notification actually calls the web service (rather than running in simulation mode), it would **close the order in the MarcomCentral store**, and the **status of each item in the order would change to "Shipped"** [mcc_o_featov.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Expanding What the Notification Sends

Beyond just the order ID, you can extend the payload. Specifically:

> To send **more closeout information** to MarcomCentral, you can add appropriate XML to the **Request payload property** of the notification. For example, you can add XML for:
> - **Invoicing**
> - **Packing slips**
> - **Settlements**

[mcc_c_PrepToSendStatus.pdf, Page 1] and [mcc_c_PrepToCallWebServices.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Alternatives for Handling Invoicing and Settlements

Two main alternatives exist:

#### Option 1: Add XML Directly to the Notification Payload
As noted above, you can include invoicing, packing slip, and settlement information directly in the **Request payload property** of the MarcomCloseoutOrder notification [mcc_c_PrepToCallWebServices.pdf, Page 1].

#### Option 2: Call Individual Web Services Separately
As an alternative, you can handle these operations **individually** by calling the dedicated MarcomCentral web services:
- **Invoice** web service
- **Packing Slip** web service
- **Settlement** web service

These can be called from either:
- A **CallSOAPService step** within your order or job ticket workflow, or
- A separate **SOAP web service notification**

For details on these individual web services, you should refer to the **MarcomCentral web services documentation** [mcc_c_PrepToCallWebServices.pdf, Page 1].

#### Option 3: Use a CallSOAPService Step Instead of a Notification
Rather than using a notification at all, you can use a **CallSOAPService step** to call the Order Closeout web service. This step would be placed in your order workflow **after the WaitForRelatedJobs step** [mcc_c_PrepToSendStatus.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Summary Table

| Approach | Method | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Default notification | MarcomCloseoutOrder sends order ID | Order closeout only |
| Extended notification payload | Add XML to Request payload | Invoicing, packing slips, settlements |
| Individual web service calls | CallSOAPService step or notification | Invoice, Packing Slip, Settlement separately |
| Alternative to notification | CallSOAPService step post-WaitForRelatedJobs | Order closeout |

Answer:

## Automatic Re-enabling of Printers After System Restart

Yes, there is a setting available to handle this exact situation. Here is what you need to know and how to configure it:

---

### Why This Happens

After a system shutdown and restart, **all printers are disabled by default** in RICOH ProcessDirector. [aiw00a12.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Solution: Enable the "Remember Enabled Status of Printers" Setting

You can configure RICOH ProcessDirector to automatically re-enable all printers that were active before the shutdown by changing the **"Remember enabled status of printers"** system property to **Yes**. [aiw00p19.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

1. Log in to the **RICOH ProcessDirector** web interface.
2. Navigate to the **Administration** tab.
3. Go to **Settings → System** page. [aiw00p18.pdf, Page 1]
4. Locate the property called **"Remember enabled status of printers"**.
5. Change its value to **Yes**. [aiw00a13.pdf, Page 1]
6. Save your changes.

---

### Result

Once this property is set to **Yes**, the next time the system is restarted, all printers that were enabled **before** the shutdown will be **automatically re-enabled** after the system comes back up. [aiw00a12.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

# Deactivating RICOH ProcessDirector Autostart on Linux

## Does the system need to be shut down first?

**No** — RICOH ProcessDirector can be **running** when you deactivate the autostart script. There is no requirement to shut down the system beforehand. [aiw00a37.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Steps to Stop RICOH ProcessDirector from Starting Automatically at Boot

Follow these steps to deactivate the autostart script:

### Step 1: Log in as Root
Log in to the Linux server as the **root user**. [aiw00a37.pdf, Page 1]

### Step 2: Open the Command Line
Access the command line interface. [aiw00a37.pdf, Page 1]

### Step 3: Identify the Symbolic Links to Remove
Navigate to the init.d directory and list the relevant links by entering these commands:

```bash
cd /etc/init.d
ls rc*/*aiwserv
```

This will display files with names like:
- `rcn.d/Snnaiwserv`
- `rcn.d/Knnaiwserv`

> ⚠️ **Important:** Note the values of **n** and **nn** (the numbers in the filenames) before deleting, as you will need them if you ever want to **reactivate** the autostart script later. [aiw00a37.pdf, Page 1]

### Step 4: Delete the Symbolic Links
Delete the files identified in the previous step (those matching the patterns `rcn.d/Snnaiwserv` and `rcn.d/Knnaiwserv`). [aiw00a37.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Additional Notes

- This procedure applies to the **base product and secondary servers** on Linux. [aiw00a37.pdf, Page 1]
- By default, when RICOH ProcessDirector is installed, the autostart script is **activated automatically**. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]
- If you ever need to **re-enable** autostart, you can reactivate the script using the `ln -s` commands to recreate the symbolic links, using the numbers you noted. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]
- **Application servers** (Windows) behave differently — they must always be started manually and are not configured via this autostart script. [aiwastartingstopping.pdf, Page 1]

## SSH Key Formats Supported for SFTP Key-Based Authentication in ProcessDirector

When setting up SSH key-based authentication for SFTP access in RICOH ProcessDirector, the following private key formats are supported:

1. **OpenSSL (traditional SSLeay) format**
2. **PKCS#8 format**

These formats are used with **SSH Key credentials**, which are a specific credential type designed for input devices and steps that require access to SFTP servers. [rcm_credentialsoverview.pdf, Page 1]

### How It Works

- You create a **Credential object** of type **SSH Key** and supply a private key in one of the two supported formats. [rcm_credentialsoverview.pdf, Page 1]
- Once created, the credential can be referenced by multiple input devices or steps that access the same SFTP site, so you only need to define the authentication information once. [rcm_credentialsoverview.pdf, Page 1]
- If the credentials change, you simply update the Credential object and the new values are automatically applied everywhere it is used. [rcm_credentialsoverview.pdf, Page 1]

### Note on Key Generation Tools
Different utility programs are available on each operating system to generate SSH keys in the supported formats. You should use the appropriate tool for your OS to generate a compatible private key. [rcm_credentialsoverview.pdf, Page 1]

# Routing Child Jobs to Separate Email and Print Branches After UpdateDocumentsInDatabase

Here is a step-by-step guide to set up conditional routing for child jobs after the **UpdateDocumentsInDatabase** step:

---

## Step 1: Set Up the SetDocPropsFromConditions Step

Add a **SetDocPropsFromConditions** step at the start of the child job branch (early in the workflow, after the `SetJobPropsFromTextFile` step). This step assigns a value to a job property based on the value of the `Pull document` (`Doc.Pull`) document property [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].

Create a **property conditions file** with the following contents:

```
"Doc.Pull","Job.Info.Attr1"
"=YES","Pull"
"=NO","Print"
```

This sets the **Custom 1** job property (`Job.Info.Attr1`) to either `Pull` or `Print` depending on whether the document was pulled [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].

---

## Step 2: Add the Email Branch Connector

After the **UpdateDocumentsInDatabase** step, add a connector leading to the **EmailDocuments** step. Apply the following rule to this connector:

> **Custom 1 = Pull**

This routes child jobs containing pulled documents to the email branch [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].

---

## Step 3: Add the Print Branch Connector

After the **UpdateDocumentsInDatabase** step, add a second connector leading to the **CreatePageRanges** step (which then connects to **PrintJobs**). Apply the following rule to this connector:

> **Custom 1 = Print**

This routes child jobs containing documents to be printed to the print branch [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].

---

## How It Works at Runtime

When child jobs reach the **SetDocPropsFromConditions** step, RICOH ProcessDirector evaluates the `Doc.Pull` property and sets `Custom 1` accordingly:

- **Child job with `Doc.Pull = YES`** → `Custom 1` is set to `Pull` → job travels through the connector with rule `Custom 1 = Pull` → routed to **EmailDocuments** [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].
- **Child job with `Doc.Pull = NO`** → `Custom 1` is set to `Print` → job travels through the connector with rule `Custom 1 = Print` → routed to **CreatePageRanges** and then **PrintJobs** [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].

---

## Step 4: Merge Branches Before Completion (Optional but Recommended)

To send parent and child jobs together to the **RetainCompletedJobs** step:

1. Add a **WaitForRelatedJobs** step before `RetainCompletedJobs`.
2. Connect all three branches to it:
   - The **parent job** branch (e.g., from `CreateJobsFromDocuments`)
   - The **pulled documents** child branch (e.g., from `EmailDocuments`)
   - The **print** child branch (e.g., from `PrintJobs`) [doc_c_createworkflow_pull.pdf, Page 4].

---

## Summary of Key Rules

| Connector From | Connector To | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| UpdateDocumentsInDatabase | EmailDocuments | Custom 1 = Pull |
| UpdateDocumentsInDatabase | CreatePageRanges | Custom 1 = Print |

Sets the **Customer name** property to `RicohSample` and the **Custom 1** property to `RicohCustom` for each retrieved JSON job. [ws-inputdevice_c_RunRestWebServWF.pdf, Page 1]

Converts the incoming JSON job order into XML format for further processing. [ws-inputdevice_c_RunRestWebServWF.pdf, Page 1]

Listed as one of the example steps demonstrated in the workflow. [ws-inputdevice_c_setupWebServices.pdf, Page 1]

Used to download print files (**Brochure.pdf** and **Cover.pdf**) locally from `http://localhost:15080/restapi/`. [ws-inputdevice_c_RunRestWebServWF.pdf, Page 1] [ws-inputdevice_c_setupWebServices.pdf, Page 1]

## AFP Indexer – Page-Level Index Tag: Advanced Tab Threshold Setting

### What the Threshold Controls

The threshold setting on the **Advanced tab** controls how far a text value can be from its original location on the page and still be recognized as a valid index tag. [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

This is necessary because, although text may appear to be in the same position on each page, **slight positional variations can occur in the AFP file**. The threshold defines the acceptable distance — both **vertically and horizontally** — from the original location. [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

> **Example:** A threshold value of **12** means the index tag can be located within **.12 of an inch** or **12 millimeters** of the original position, in either direction. [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Available Range of Values

You can select from the following ranges:

| Measurement Unit | Range |
|---|---|
| **Inches** | 1/100 to 1 inch |
| **Millimeters** | 1 to 25 millimeters |

[definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Default Values & Important Warning

- The **default threshold value** is typically sufficient: **10** (for inches) or **2** (for millimeters). [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]
- ⚠️ **Caution:** If you increase the threshold above the default, you risk creating **unexpected index tags**, because the match is based **only on location** — the first text block found within the threshold range will be used as the index tag. [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

---

> 💡 **Tip:** You can switch measurement units between inches and millimeters by clicking **View ⇒ Units** in RICOH Visual Workbench. [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

## AFP Indexer: Custom Page Groups vs. Embedded AFP Page Groups

Yes — when you create custom page groups in AFP Indexer, the page groups already embedded in the AFP file are **overridden and ignored**. Here is a detailed breakdown:

---

### What Happens When You Create New Page Groups

When you define new page groups in AFP Indexer (either fixed-length or trigger-based), **any existing page groups defined in the AFP file itself are not used**. [creatingpagegroupscontainer.pdf, Page 1] [indexingafpfiles.pdf, Page 1]

More specifically:

- If you create page groups using **triggers** or create page groups of **fixed length**, **all existing page groups AND index tags** that are defined in the AFP file itself are **ignored**. [pagegroups_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Your Options When an AFP File Already Contains Page Groups

You are not forced to override the existing page groups. AFP Indexer gives you a choice:

1. **Use the existing page groups** embedded in the AFP file — In most cases, if an AFP file contains page groups, you should use them. If you use the existing page groups, you cannot change the page group boundaries, but you can create additional index tags and modify existing tag values. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Create new page groups** (fixed-length or trigger-based) — This will cause the embedded page groups and index tags to be ignored entirely. [creatingpagegroupscontainer.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Use Existing Page Groups (Step-by-Step)

If you want to **preserve** the AFP file's embedded page groups instead of overriding them:

1. In **RICOH Visual Workbench**, open a sample AFP file, then click **Mode → AFP Indexer**. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]
2. Click **Tools → Other Page Groups → Use Existing Page Groups**. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]
3. If prompted with a warning about page groups and indexes changing, click **Yes**. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]
4. In the **Use page group level** field, select a number (0–20) for the level of the page group structure you want to keep. Select **0** to keep all page group levels. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]
5. To remove existing index tags from the AFP file, clear the **Use index tags** box. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]
6. Click **OK**. [importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Action Taken in AFP Indexer | Effect on Embedded AFP Page Groups |
|---|---|
| Create fixed-length page groups | Embedded page groups & index tags **ignored** |
| Create trigger-based page groups | Embedded page groups & index tags **ignored** |
| Use Existing Page Groups option | Embedded page groups **preserved** (boundaries cannot be changed) |
| No action taken | Existing page groups and index tags **are used by default** |

[importingexistingdefinitions.pdf, Page 1] [pagegroups_overview.pdf, Page 1]

## AFP Indexer: Behavior with a Single Street Line Instead of Two

When AFP Indexer is configured to tag intermediate address lines (such as street lines), it handles variable numbers of intermediate lines gracefully.

**Specifically, if a page group only has one street line instead of two, AFP Indexer will only create the index tag for that single existing line — it will NOT create an index tag for the non-existent second line.**

This is explicitly documented:

> *"AFP Indexer does not create index tags for intermediate lines that do not exist in a page group. For example, if the address in a particular page group does not contain the second intermediate line in the street address, AFP Indexer only creates index tag 'Street1'."*
> [creatingindexesinaddressarea.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Summary of Behavior

| Scenario | Index Tags Created |
|---|---|
| Page group has **two** street lines | `Street1` **and** `Street2` |
| Page group has **only one** street line | `Street1` **only** |

So in short, AFP Indexer automatically adapts to the actual number of intermediate lines present in each page group, skipping index tag creation for any lines that simply do not exist in that particular page group. [creatingindexesinaddressarea.pdf, Page 2]

## Recovering from an Unplanned Primary Server Outage

### Reconnection Frequency

When the primary server suffers an unplanned outage, any application/secondary server that is defined to it will **attempt to reestablish the connection every 30 seconds**, continuing until it is able to connect or until it stops. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1] [aiw00a36.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Correct Order of Steps to Bring Everything Back Up

Before following these steps, ensure that all problems on the primary computer have been fixed and that it is available on the network. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]

1. **Stop each secondary server** installed on another (remote) computer using the `stopaiw` command. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Stop any application servers** that are running. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
3. **Stop the base product** using the `stopaiw` command. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
4. **Start the base product and any secondary servers on the same computer** using the `startaiw` command. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
5. **Verify that secondary servers running on the same computer** as the base product are **enabled**. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
6. **Start each secondary server installed on another (remote) computer** using the `startaiw` command. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
7. **Start any application servers** that were previously stopped. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
8. **Enable the application and secondary servers** that were just started. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
9. **Enable and start your printers**. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]
10. **Enable and connect your input devices**. [aiw00a43.pdf, Page 1]

---

> **💡 Tip:** Note that after a system shutdown and restart, all printers are disabled by default. If you want printers that were enabled before the shutdown to be automatically re-enabled after restart, you can set the **"Remember enabled status of printers"** system property to **Yes**. Answer:

## Why You Should Leave the File Patterns Property Blank When Using lpr or lprafp

When submitting jobs to an LPD input device using the `lpr` or `lprafp` command, you should leave the **File patterns** property blank on expected work objects for the following reason:

The `lpr` or `lprafp` command **renames the input file** using a format that RICOH ProcessDirector **cannot reliably parse**. [sla_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]

Because the input file name is renamed in an unpredictable way, the expected work object would be unable to correctly match the file name against any regular expression pattern you define in the **File patterns** property. [sla_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommended Approach

Instead of relying on file name pattern matching, follow this guidance:

1. **Use only the Number of jobs expected property** on your expected work objects to count arriving jobs. [sla_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Leave the File patterns property blank** so that the input device does not attempt to parse the renamed file names. [sla_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]

This ensures that the expected work object can still accurately count and monitor incoming jobs against your defined schedule — for example, to support SLA monitoring — without failing due to unparseable file names. [sla_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]

## Capturing a Multi-Word City Name with Substring by Delimiter

To capture the city name "Eldorado Springs" from the address `Eldorado Springs CO 80025` using a blank space as the delimiter, configure the settings as follows:

---

### Required Settings

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Delimiter** | Blank character (space) |
| **Starting From** | End of Line |
| **First Position** | **3** |
| **Number to Retain** | **10** |

---

### Step-by-Step Explanation

1. **Set the Delimiter** to a blank character (space). This splits the address into four separate segments:
   - Segment 1: `Eldorado`
   - Segment 2: `Springs`
   - Segment 3: `CO`
   - Segment 4: `80025`

   [pdfw_t_plugin_adddocprops.pdf, Page 2]

2. **Select "End of Line"** from the Starting From drop-down menu. [pdfw_t_plugin_adddocprops.pdf, Page 2]

3. **Set First Position to `3`** — this tells the system to start counting from the 3rd delimiter segment from the end of the line (i.e., the beginning of the city name). [pdfw_t_plugin_adddocprops.pdf, Page 2]

4. **Set Number to Retain to `10`** — by specifying 10, you ensure that city names containing **up to ten words** are fully captured, accommodating multi-word city names like "Eldorado Springs". [pdfw_t_plugin_adddocprops.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Why Number to Retain = 10?

> *"By specifying 10 for Number to Retain, you can select city names with up to ten words."*
> [pdfw_t_plugin_addmultidocprops.pdf, Page 2]

This is the recommended approach precisely because city names can consist of multiple words. Setting a high Number to Retain (like 10) ensures the full city name is always captured regardless of how many words it contains. [pdfw_t_plugin_addbarcode.pdf, Page 4]

## Step Template Using the Enhance AFP Control File with Updated Address Data and Document Property Definitions

Based on the evidence provided, when setting up postal enablement for AFP files, the step templates that use the Enhance AFP control file are clearly documented.

### Step Templates That Use the EnhanceAFP Control File

The following step templates use the EnhanceAFP control file to change the content of AFP files [vwb_EnhancerOverview.pdf, Page 1]:

1. **`BuildAFPFromDocuments`**
   - A step based on this template creates an AFP file for a job
   - If barcodes, text, and hidden areas are defined in an EnhanceAFP control file, this step applies them
   - The AFP file produced becomes the AFP file for subsequent steps in the workflow

2. **`CreateAFPJobsFromDocuments`**
   - A step based on this template generates one or more child AFP jobs
   - If barcodes, text, and hidden areas are defined in an EnhanceAFP control file, this step applies them

3. **`BuildEnhanceAFPFile`** *(for Advanced Document Pool only)*
   - Requires the Document Pool extended feature
   - Creates a control file that manages enhancements so that some documents have **different enhancements than other documents** [vwb_EnhancerOverview.pdf, Page 1]

### Context Within Postal Enablement Setup

The Enhance AFP control file itself is created using the **AFP Enhancer mode** in RICOH Visual Workbench, and it is used to:
- Create a barcode with **updated mailing address data** returned by the postal software
- **Replace** the original mailing address data with updated data returned by the postal software
- Hide areas that contain unwanted content [mail_c_EnhanceAFP.pdf, Page 1]

The control file is exported via **Tools ⇒ Export EnhanceAFP Control File** and sent to the RICOH ProcessDirector server before being referenced in the applicable step [mail_c_EnhanceAFP.pdf, Page 1].
