## Purpose of a Service Policy Object in RICOH ProcessDirector

Based on the provided documentation, here is a comprehensive explanation of the purpose and definition of a service policy object:

---

### Purpose

A **service policy object** in RICOH ProcessDirector is used to define **checkpoints and a deadline for jobs**. Its primary purpose is to help you monitor whether jobs are on schedule to meet the performance commitments outlined in a **Service Level Agreement (SLA)**. [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What a Service Policy Defines

A service policy defines the following key elements:

1. **Checkpoints** – These are milestones that allow you to track the progress of jobs as they flow through the system, helping you determine if jobs are on schedule to meet SLA commitments. [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]

2. **SLA Deadline** – This represents the ultimate goal of the SLA; the service policy calculates the planned checkpoints and the SLA deadline for all jobs that use an associated workflow. [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]

3. **No-Service Periods** – The service policy can be configured to adjust job checkpoints for periods when services are not provided (e.g., holidays and weekends). These periods are defined in **no-service period objects**. [slapolicy.pdf, Page 1]

4. **Time Zone** – The service policy specifies the time zone where jobs are printed. If jobs are printed across multiple time zones, a separate service policy must be created for each time zone. [slapolicy.pdf, Page 1]

5. **Checkpoint Status** – RICOH ProcessDirector periodically calculates a checkpoint status for each job as it progresses through the system, helping identify jobs that are late in meeting their checkpoints. [slapolicy.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Additional Notes

- Service policies are **associated with workflows**; each workflow can have **one associated service policy**, and the policy applies to all jobs using that workflow. [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]
- Service policies are **not used** when tracking to a schedule based on estimated durations or to a deadline set by a `SetDeadline` step or the **Change Deadline** action. [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]
- RICOH ProcessDirector provides **predefined (sample) service policies** (e.g., *3-day cutoff* and *24 hour*) that can be used, modified, or deleted as needed. [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]

The file must be renamed so that it contains the name of the AFP code page, using the `.cp` file extension.

If the name of the AFP code page is **T1000259**, you would rename the file to:

## Xerox PDF Printer: "All Media" vs. Specific Media Objects for Scheduling

When configuring the **Media supported** property on the Scheduling tab of a Xerox PDF printer in ProcessDirector, the choice you make directly controls which jobs can be assigned to that printer. Here is a breakdown of each option:

---

### Option 1: All Media

If you choose **All media**, **all jobs can be scheduled to the printer, regardless of what media is actually loaded** in it. [xrx_c_Define_XeroxPDF.pdf, Page 1]

- This means ProcessDirector will not filter or restrict job assignment based on media requirements.
- Jobs requesting any type of media will be eligible to print on this printer.

---

### Option 2: Specific Media Objects

If you choose **specific media objects**, **only jobs that use that media can be scheduled to this printer**. [xrx_c_Define_XeroxPDF.pdf, Page 1]

- ProcessDirector will match the media requested by a job against the media objects you selected.
- Jobs requiring different media will **not** be scheduled to this printer.

---

### Option 3: Ready Media Objects (also available)

There is a third option worth noting: if you choose **Ready media objects**, **only jobs that require the media currently loaded in the printer** can be scheduled to it. [xrx_c_Define_XeroxPDF.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Setting | Jobs Scheduled |
|---|---|
| **All media** | All jobs, regardless of media loaded |
| **Specific media** | Only jobs requesting those exact media objects |
| **Ready media** | Only jobs matching media currently loaded in the printer |

---

### Key Tip

When configuring the Scheduling tab, you should **leave values blank or set to "Not set"** for any properties that should not be used for scheduling — those values will match any corresponding job scheduling property values. [xrx_c_Define_XeroxPDF.pdf, Page 1]

## RICOH ProcessDirector: Child Job Storage & Default Spool Directory

### Default Spool Directory Path Format

When RICOH ProcessDirector creates a job from an input file, it creates a unique spool directory. The default spool directory for a job follows this format:

```
/aiw/aiw1/spool/default/JobNumber
```

Where **JobNumber** is the spool ID that RICOH ProcessDirector assigns to the job. [aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

> **Note for Application Servers (Windows):** On an application server, the spool directory is mounted on the drive chosen during installation. The default Windows path is:
> ```
> Z:\aiw1\spool\default\JobNumber
> ```
> [aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

You can also create **additional spool directories** with names in this format:
```
/aiw/aiw1/spool/SpoolName/JobNumber
```
Where **SpoolName** is the subdirectory name defined by an authorized user. [aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Where Child Jobs Are Stored

Child jobs created by an external program are stored in a **`children` subdirectory** within the job's spool directory. The path follows one of these two formats depending on which spool directory is in use:

| Spool Type | Child Job Path |
|---|---|
| Default spool | `/aiw/aiw1/spool/default/JobNumber/children` |
| Custom spool | `/aiw/aiw1/spool/SpoolName/JobNumber/children` |

[aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Child Job File Naming Format

When the external program writes child-job files to the `children` subdirectory, the file names must follow this specific format:

```
JobNumber.UsageType.DataType.n,Job.JobType=WorkflowName
```

Where **WorkflowName** is the name of the workflow the child job requires. That workflow must exist and be enabled. [aiwcstextstepnothot.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How RICOH ProcessDirector Processes Child Jobs

After RICOH ProcessDirector **detects the child jobs and their associated files** in the `children` subdirectory, it continues to process them automatically. [aiw00c16.pdf, Page 1]

## Setting Up Different Printers for Two RetainCompletedJobs Branches

You are experiencing expected system behavior. The **RetainCompletedJobs** step template does **not** use positional properties, which means that when you change a property value on one step based on that template, it changes on **all** steps based on the same template in the workflow. [aiw_o_PositionalJobProperties.pdf, Page 1]

### Why This Happens

The **Requested printer** job property is shared across all steps based on the same step template within a workflow. As documented:

> *"If you change the value of the Requested printer property for one step from PrinterBldg1 to PrinterBldg2, the value of the property for the other step changes to PrinterBldg2."* [aiw_o_PositionalJobProperties.pdf, Page 1]

---

### The Solution: Use AssignJobValues Steps

To send jobs in each branch to a **different printer**, you must place a step based on the **AssignJobValues** step template **before each RetainCompletedJobs step** in each branch. Here is how to set it up:

**Step-by-step instructions:**

1. **In Branch 1** of your conditional workflow, add a step based on the **AssignJobValues** step template immediately before the **RetainCompletedJobs** step.
2. On that **AssignJobValues** step, set the **Requested printer** property to the printer you want for Branch 1 (e.g., `PrinterBldg1`).
3. **In Branch 2**, add another step based on the **AssignJobValues** step template immediately before its **RetainCompletedJobs** step.
4. On that **AssignJobValues** step, set the **Requested printer** property to the printer you want for Branch 2 (e.g., `PrinterBldg2`).
5. Save and enable the workflow.

The value set in each **AssignJobValues** step will **override** the Requested printer property value on the RetainCompletedJobs steps. [aiw_c_hintssteptemplates.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_o_PositionalJobProperties.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Principle to Remember

- Step templates with **positional properties** (e.g., RunExternalProgram) allow each instance to have independent values. [aiw_o_PositionalJobProperties.pdf, Page 1]
- Step templates **without** positional properties (e.g., **RetainCompletedJobs**, **PrintJobs**) share values across all instances — so **AssignJobValues** is always the correct workaround for branch-specific printer assignments. [aiw_c_hintssteptemplates.pdf, Page 1]

## Using a Single Data Collector for Both Reports in ProcessDirector

**Yes, you can use a single data collector for both reports.** According to the documentation, a printing company facing exactly this scenario was able to collect data for both reports using one data collector.

---

### Which Data Collector to Use

You should use the **Job Print Progress data collector** (also referred to as "Job Print Status" in the data collectors list). A single instance of this data collector can supply data for both the "pages per printer" and "jobs per customer" reports simultaneously. [reportsPostgresql_o_scen_Reports.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Which Job Properties to Select

In the data collector's **"Job properties to capture"** list, you need to select the following **four properties** — two for each report:

| Report | Required Properties |
|---|---|
| **Pages printed by printer** | `Pages stacked` and `Previous Printer` |
| **Jobs printed by customer** | `Job number` and `Customer name` |

So the complete set of properties to select is:
1. **Pages stacked**
2. **Previous Printer**
3. **Job number**
4. **Customer name**

[reportsPostgresql_o_scen_Reports.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Steps to Configure the Data Collector

1. Click the **Administration** tab. [reportsPostgresql_c_CaptureDataForPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]
2. In the left pane, click **Reports ⇒ Data Collectors**. [reportsPostgresql_c_CaptureDataForPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]
3. Open the **Job Print Progress** data collector. [reportsPostgresql_o_scen_Reports.pdf, Page 1]
4. In the **Job properties to capture** list, select the four properties listed above. [reportsPostgresql_o_scen_Reports.pdf, Page 1]
5. Name the database table (e.g., `job_printing`). [reportsPostgresql_o_scen_Reports.pdf, Page 1]
6. Click the **switch at the top of the dialog** to enable the data collector. [reportsPostgresql_c_CaptureDataForPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]
7. Click **OK**. ProcessDirector will then capture the property values in the PostgreSQL database each time a job **starts or stops printing**. [reportsPostgresql_o_scen_Reports.pdf, Page 1]

> **Note:** Data collection must be enabled globally for data collectors to store information in the database. If data collection is disabled, enabled data collectors will do nothing. [reportsPostgresql_c_CaptureDataForPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]

## File Format Restriction for the Pages Batching Method on SFTP Input Devices

When using the **Pages batching method** on an SFTP input device, the following file format restrictions apply:

---

### 1. **PDF Files Only**
The Pages batching method is **only valid for PDF files**. The input device examines PDF files as they arrive and determines how many pages they contain. [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1]

The **Data patterns** property must be configured with a pattern that matches PDF file names, such as `.*pdf$` or `.*PDF$`. [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. **No Encrypted or Password-Protected PDF Files**
The Pages batching method **does not support encrypted or password-protected PDF files**. If an encrypted or password-protected PDF file is submitted to a hot folder or SFTP input device that uses the Pages batching method, **RICOH ProcessDirector will issue an error message** because it cannot open the file to count the number of pages. [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1]

---

| Restriction | Detail |
|---|---|
| Supported format | PDF files only |
| Unsupported files | Encrypted or password-protected PDFs |

These two restrictions together define the complete file format requirements when using the Pages batching method on an SFTP input device. [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1]

## Handling an Account Number Split Across Two AFP Text Blocks

When an account number is split across two separate text blocks on the same line, you can handle this by creating an **index tag within an index area** that spans both text blocks and concatenates their values into a single index tag.

---

### Why This Works

The AFP Indexer supports creating index tags that span multiple text blocks on the same line. As stated in the documentation:

> "If one text block on a line contains the first half of an account number and the next text block on the line contains the second half of the account number, you can concatenate the values in the text blocks and create one index tag that spans both blocks of text."

[indextags_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

**Step 1: Open the AFP file in AFP Indexer mode**
In RICOH Visual Workbench, open the sample AFP file containing the account number, then click **Mode ⇒ AFP Indexer**. [creatingindexesinarea.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 2: Draw a box around both text blocks**
Position your cursor at a corner of the area that contains **both** text blocks of the account number. While pressing the left mouse button, draw a box that includes the first character of each AFP text block you want to index. The area does not need to include all characters in the text blocks. [creatingindexesinarea.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 3: Open the Create Index Tags window**
Right-click anywhere on the page and click **Create Index Tags**. The **Create Index Tags in an Area** window will appear. [creatingindexesinarea.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 4: Verify the text**
Check that both portions of the account number are shown in the **Lines in the area** field. If not, click **Cancel** and redraw the area, or use the **Position tab** to adjust the origin and size of the index area. [creatingindexesinarea.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 5: Configure concatenation**
When creating the single index tag, specify how the text from the two blocks should be joined. You can:
- **Concatenate directly** (e.g., `"123"` + `"45678"` → `"12345678"`)
- **Separate with a blank** (e.g., `"123 45678"`)
- **Separate with any other character** (e.g., `"123-45678"`)

[creatingindexesinarea.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Requirement

> "The index area must include the **first character** in each AFP text block that you want to index; however, the area does not need to include all the characters in the AFP text blocks."

[creatingindexesinarea.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Result

The two separate text blocks will be merged into **one single index tag**, representing the complete account number, ready for indexing across all page groups.

## Parameters for `sftp_file.sh` — Sending an Inserter Control File to a Remote Host

Based on the documentation, here is a breakdown of the **required** versus **optional** parameters when using `sftp_file.sh` to send an inserter control file:

---

### ✅ Required Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `-d destination_directory/filename` | Specifies the destination directory and file name of the inserter control file on the remote host. You may use a RICOH ProcessDirector symbol (e.g., `${Job.Inserter.JobID}`) in the file name. |
| `-h host` | Specifies the host name of the remote (separate) computer. |
| `-u user_id` | Specifies the login name on the remote computer. |
| `-x put` | Indicates that the inserter control file is to be **sent** from RICOH ProcessDirector to another system. |

[UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 2]

---

### ⚙️ Optional Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `-p file_permissions` | Specifies the permissions (in octal format) to set on the inserter control file in the destination directory using the UNIX `chmod` command. If omitted, no permissions are set. |
| `-v` | Enables **verbose mode** to assist with troubleshooting. |

[UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 2], [UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 3]

---

### ⚠️ Important Notes

1. **Brackets in the documentation indicate optional parameters.** The full send command syntax is:
   ```
   sftp_file.sh -d destination_directory/filename -h host [-p file_permissions] -u user_id [-v] -x put
   ```
   [UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 2]

2. **Do NOT specify any additional parameters** beyond those listed above. For example, do not specify the `-s` parameter (used for source directory/filename in receive operations) when sending. [UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 2]

3. **Prerequisites:** The **Secure Shell (SSH)** and **SFTP** commands must be installed on the Linux system. You can verify this by running `which ssh` and `which sftp` on the command line. [UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 2]

4. Note that unlike `ftp_file.sh`, the `sftp_file.sh` send command does **not** include a `-w password` parameter in its syntax, reflecting SFTP's use of key-based or other authentication methods. [UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 2]

## Why Inline Resources Aren't Showing in Output — and How to Fix It

### Root Cause

When you submit line data jobs with inline resources (such as page definitions) to a workflow that uses the **ConvertLineDataJobIntoAFP** step, most inline resources are **ignored by default**. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]

This happens because the **Resource type** property for the ConvertLineDataJobIntoAFP step is pre-configured with these values: **Form definition, Fonts, Inline**. The value **"Inline"** tells RICOH ProcessDirector to keep *only* inline form definitions and fonts — and to **not write any other inline resources** (such as page definitions) from the data stream to the output file. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]

So even if AFP Download Plus or Download for z/OS includes page definitions or other resources inline with the job, RICOH ProcessDirector will not write them to the output file. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Fix It

You need to update the **Resource type** property on the ConvertLineDataJobIntoAFP step in your workflow. Follow these steps:

1. **Click the Workflow tab.** [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Click the name of the workflow** you want to edit (for example, *DownloadLineData*). [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
3. *(Optional)* **Disable the workflow** by clicking the switch to the left of the workflow name. If you do not disable it while editing, jobs using this workflow will continue to move through steps. When you save, the workflow is momentarily disabled then re-enabled — jobs currently processing could move into error. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
4. **Right-click the ConvertLineDataJobIntoAFP step** and select **Properties**. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
5. **Click AFP.** In the **Resource type** field, you will see a list of resources with *Inline* and *Form definition* already selected. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
6. **Add the additional inline resource types** you need (e.g., Page definitions) by **holding the Ctrl key** and selecting them from the list. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
7. **Click OK.** [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]
8. **Save and enable the workflow** by changing the Save & Enable/Disable switch to the **On** position. [aiwj_inlineresources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Page definitions not in output | "Inline" value limits resources to fonts & form definitions only | Add Page definitions (and others as needed) to the Resource type property |

---

### ✅ Solución recomendada

**Incluir la ruta completa a Quadient Inspire Designer en la propiedad "External command"** en todos los lugares donde aparezca.

> *"If you cannot edit the PATH, you must include the full path to Quadient Inspire Designer in the External command property wherever it appears."*

---

### Pasos de configuración adicionales requeridos

Independientemente de la solución del PATH, cada flujo de trabajo AFP requiere los siguientes objetos del sistema:

1. **Un dispositivo de entrada apropiado** — Se recomienda copiar uno de los dispositivos de carpeta activa (hot folder) suministrados con la función:
   - `HotFolderReformatAFP`
   - `HotFolderComposeAFPDataSubmitted`
   - `HotFolderComposeAFPDataRetrieved`

   Todos estos dispositivos tienen el **método de agrupación (Batching method)** configurado como **List**. Si solo vas a enviar un archivo WFD como trabajo de impresión, cambia el método de agrupación a **None**. [aiw_gmc_configforprintnet.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Un paso basado en la plantilla de paso `ComposeAFP`** [aiw_gmc_configforprintnet.pdf, Page 1]

Puedes copiar y personalizar uno de los siguientes flujos de trabajo AFP disponibles cuando las funciones **Quadient Inspire Connect** y **AFP Support** están instaladas:

| Flujo de trabajo | Cuándo usarlo |
|---|---|

## TotalFlow Print Server – Job Moved to Inactive Jobs

Based on the provided documentation, here is a complete answer to your question:

---

### Job State in ProcessDirector

When TotalFlow Print Server is controlling the printer and a user moves a job from the **Active Jobs** state to the **Inactive Jobs** state on the printer console (or deletes the job from the printer), **RICOH ProcessDirector changes the state of the job to "Status changed on printer."** [aiw_ConfigVC60000.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How an Operator Can Resend or Continue the Job

Once the job is in the **"Status changed on printer"** state, an operator has the following options [aiw_ConfigVC60000.pdf, Page 1]:

1. **Print again / Restart step action**
   - Right-click the job in RICOH ProcessDirector.
   - Select **Print again** or **Restart step** to resend the job to the printer.

2. **Go to next step action** *(only if the job already printed successfully)*
   - Right-click the job in RICOH ProcessDirector.
   - Select **Go to next step** to continue processing the job through the rest of the workflow, without resending it to the printer.

---

### Additional Context

For reference, when TotalFlow Print Server is set up to control the printer (as opposed to RICOH ProcessDirector controlling it), RICOH ProcessDirector spools the PDF jobs to the printer and the operator uses the TotalFlow Print Server console to release them. While in this spooled state, the job shows as **"Spooled at printer"** in RICOH ProcessDirector. [aiw_ConfigVC60000.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ **Note:** If RICOH ProcessDirector itself is restarted while jobs are in the **"Spooled at printer"** state, those jobs will change to **Error** state — and they may have already printed. [aiw_ConfigVC60000.pdf, Page 1]

These phases help to organize the path that jobs take through the system. Jobs can flow through all the phases or through a few of the phases. The addition of features to the base RICOH ProcessDirector product might add additional phases to the workflow. The default phase names can be changed to better match the functions that you perform in that phase. Steps in the phases do the actual phase work. The workflow determines which phases the job passes through and the order of the steps in each phase. The processing phases in the base product are: Receive phase In the Receive phase, the RICOH ProcessDirector system accepts input files for processing. Each job is assigned a workflow, which defines the phases and steps that process the job. Steps in the Receive phase also set the initial values of job properties for use by later steps in the workflow. For example, RICOH ProcessDirector might queue the job to the first step of the Prepare phase or queue the job directly to the Print phase. After the Receive phase queues the input file, it becomes a job on the RICOH ProcessDirector system. Prepare phase The Prepare phase composes, transforms, and indexes the job to create printable pages. You can also instruct RICOH ProcessDirector to run external programs during the Prepare phase to further condition or interpret the job. Assemble phase If you have the PDF Document Support or AFP Support feature, the Assemble phase organizes documents prior to a phase such as Print that produces the physical documents. Print phase The Print phase routes and sends the job to an available printer, monitors printing status, and reports print completion. It can include a manual quality check, which can let the operator make printer adjustments prior to reprinting the job. It might also send the job to an external program for customized processing. Insert phase If you have the Inserter feature, the Insert phase communicates with the inserter controller and reconciles the job after it completes insertion. Complete phase After jobs have completed all other processing, they arrive in the Complete phase. The Complete phase manages the retention period for jobs; it deletes jobs that have no retention periods or whose retention periods have expired. For jobs that consist of a parent job and one or more child jobs, the Complete phase makes sure that no additional actions take place until all the related jobs reach the Complete phase. In the Complete phase, you can also invoke external programs on completed jobs. For example, an external program can copy the jobs to an archive system. Parent topic: Product overview


Answer:

## Parent and Child Jobs at the Final Processing Stage in RICOH ProcessDirector

When parent and child jobs reach their final processing stage in RICOH ProcessDirector, the following occurs:

---

### 1. The WaitForRelatedJobs Step

Before entering the final phase, parent and child jobs are synchronized at the **WaitForRelatedJobs** step. All related jobs must arrive at this step before processing continues:

- The child job with printed documents moves to the **WaitForRelatedJobs** step after the **PrintJobs** step. [doc_o_scen_pull_latepay.pdf, Page 2]
- The child job with email documents moves to the **WaitForRelatedJobs** step after the **EmailDocuments** step. [pref_o_scen_distribute.pdf, Page 3]
- The child job with Web documents moves to the **WaitForRelatedJobs** step after the **RunExternalProgram** step. [pref_o_scen_distribute.pdf, Page 3]

---

### 2. Transition to the Complete Phase (RetainCompletedJobs)

Once **all** child jobs have arrived at the **WaitForRelatedJobs** step:

- **RICOH ProcessDirector sends them to the RetainCompletedJobs step.** [doc_o_scen_pull_flood.pdf, Page 2]
- In the scenario with distributed statements, **the parent job and the child jobs start their retention period** when all child jobs reach the WaitForRelatedJobs step. [pref_o_scen_distribute.pdf, Page 3]

---

### 3. The Complete Phase Behavior

In the **Complete phase**, RICOH ProcessDirector manages the retention period and ensures coordinated completion:

- The Complete phase **manages the retention period for jobs** and **deletes jobs that have no retention periods or whose retention periods have expired.** [aiw00o5.pdf, Page 1]
- Critically, for jobs consisting of a **parent job and one or more child jobs**, the Complete phase **makes sure that no additional actions take place until all the related jobs reach the Complete phase.** [aiw00o5.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Stage | What Happens |
|---|---|
| **WaitForRelatedJobs** | All parent and child jobs synchronize; none proceed until all arrive |
| **RetainCompletedJobs** | All related jobs are sent together to begin retention |
| **Complete Phase** | Retention period starts; jobs are held until all related jobs are present, then deleted upon expiry |

## IMB Serial Number File Permissions on Linux

When setting up IMB serial number files on Linux, the following permissions and access requirements apply:

### Required Permissions

The serial number file must have the **appropriate permissions set so that both of the following can read and update the file** [creatingserialfile.pdf, Page 1]:

---

### System User Access

| Access Type | Default Name |
|---|---|
| **System User** | `aiw1` |
| **Group** | `aiwgrp1` |

- The **RICOH ProcessDirector system user** (default: **`aiw1`**) must be able to **read and update** the file [creatingserialfile.pdf, Page 1].
- **All users in the RICOH ProcessDirector group** (default: **`aiwgrp1`**) must also be able to **read and update** the file [creatingserialfile.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Step-by-Step Setup (Linux)

1. **Create the serial number file** using any editor [creatingserialfile.pdf, Page 1].
2. **Name the file** based on the barcode definition name it applies to (e.g., if the barcode is named `to-imb`, name the file `to-imb-serial`) [creatingserialfile.pdf, Page 1].
3. **Set the file permissions** so that:
   - The system user `aiw1` (default) can **read and update** the file [barcode_IMBdata_tab.pdf, Page 1].
   - All users in the group `aiwgrp1` (default) can **read and update** the file [barcode_IMBreplacedata_tab.pdf, Page 1].

---

> ⚠️ **Note:** These are the **default** user and group names. Your installation may use different names if customized during setup [vwb_barcodes_overview_imb_data.pdf, Page 3].

Answer:

## Handling Multiple Sample XML Files in Order Property Mapping

You do **not** need to redo the whole mapping for each file. Here is how it works:

---

### Recommended Approach

**Step 1: Start with one file**
When you begin creating the order property mapping, select **one sample XML file first** and work through the entire setup procedure with that file. [aiw_OrdPropMap.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 2: Update the mapping with the remaining files afterward**
Once you have completed the mapping with the first file, you can **update the existing property mapping** with the other sample XML files later — you do not need to start over from scratch. [aiw_OrdPropMap.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why Multiple Files May Be Needed

The reason you might have multiple sample XML files is that **different types of orders or jobs can use different XML elements**. If you cannot include all types of orders in a single XML file, you should export multiple XML files to cover all the variations. [aiw_OrdPropMap.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Reminder

Regardless of how many files you use, the mapping must always include **at least two XML elements**:
- One to **identify orders**
- One to **identify the jobs** within that order type

The job-identifying XML element must be a **child** of the order-identifying element. [aiw_OrdPropMap.pdf, Page 1]

---

**In summary:** Work through the full procedure with one file first, then incrementally update the same mapping object with your additional sample files. No need to redo everything from scratch.

## Loading New Document Properties in the Acrobat Plug-in

Yes, after adding new document properties in ProcessDirector, you **must** perform a manual reload procedure in the Acrobat plug-in before those properties become available. Here are the steps:

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

**1. Close Adobe Acrobat Professional**
Before doing anything else, fully close Adobe Acrobat Professional. [pdfw_t_plugin_loaddocprops.pdf, Page 1]

**2. Retrieve the `definitions.zip` file from the ProcessDirector server**
Navigate to the appropriate directory on your RICOH ProcessDirector server:
- **Linux:** `/aiw/aiw1/share`
- **Windows:** `C:\aiw\aiw1\share`

**3. Place the `definitions.zip` file in the correct local directory**
On the system where the plug-in is installed, copy the file to:

*(Tip: You can find your AppData path by typing `%appdata%` in the Windows Run command line.)* [pdfw_t_plugin_loaddocprops.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Barcode Format Position for Partial Barcode Reads in Automated Verification

Great question! This is a common configuration consideration when setting up cameras or barcode scanners for Automated Verification.

### Answer

**You should specify position 1** in the barcode format for the document property, even though it starts at a different position in the full barcode.

---

### Explanation

The barcode format must match the **configuration of the camera or barcode scanner hardware**. The key rule is:

> If the camera or barcode scanner is configured to read only one property in the barcode, **specify that this property starts in position 1** in the barcode format.

[BarCodeFormatObject.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Your Specific Example

Using exactly the scenario you described:

| Scenario Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Property position in the **full** barcode | Position 10 |
| Camera configured to read | Characters 10 through 25 |
| Position to specify **in the barcode format** | **Position 1** |

The reasoning is straightforward: since the camera is only capturing characters 10–25, **from the camera's perspective, the data it delivers to RICOH ProcessDirector begins at character 1**. The barcode format must reflect what the camera actually sends, not where the data sits in the original full barcode. [BarCodeFormatObject.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Important Reminder

If you are using multiple barcode formats for the same barcode reader, the **Job number** and **Sequence in child job** properties must be in the **same positions** across all barcode formats used by that reader. [BarCodeFormatObject.pdf, Page 1]

## Native2ascii Utility Location and File Format Requirements

### Location of the `native2ascii` Utility on Linux

On a Linux system running RICOH ProcessDirector, the `native2ascii` utility is located at:

```
/opt/infoprint/ippd/jre/bin
```

[aiwdoc_i_t_editdocdefpropsfile.pdf, Page 1] [aiwdoc_i_r_supportingmorelangs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Required File Format Before Placing in the Config Directory

The `docCustomDefinitions.properties` files **must be in ISO-8859-1 character encoding format** before being placed in the configuration directory (`/aiw/aiw1/config` on Linux). Specifically:

- The files must contain **only Latin-1 or Unicode-encoded (`\udddd` notation) characters**. [aiwdoc_i_r_supportingmorelangs.pdf, Page 1]
- If the files were created in a **different format** (such as Shift JIS or UTF-8), they **must be converted to ISO-8859-1** prior to being placed in the config directory. [aiwdoc_i_t_editdocdefpropsfile.pdf, Page 2]

---

### How to Use `native2ascii` for Conversion

If your file is not already in Latin-1 or Unicode format, you can use the `native2ascii` utility to convert it. For example, to convert a UTF-8 encoded file, use the following command:

```bash
native2ascii -encoding UTF-8 docCustomDefinitions-UTF8.properties > docCustomDefinitions.properties
```

[aiwdoc_i_r_supportingmorelangs.pdf, Page 1]

> **Important:** The `native2ascii` utility converts text to Unicode Latin-1 format and is shipped with RICOH ProcessDirector. [aiwdoc_i_r_supportingmorelangs.pdf, Page 1]

Essentially, link color conversion CMRs replace a pair of color conversion CMRs. Converting color images to and from the PCS takes a significant amount of processing resources, in part because the process includes two conversions. Link color conversion CMRs combine the two conversions and make them more efficient. The printer can use the link color conversion CMR to convert colors directly from the color space of the input device to the color space of the output device with the same color fidelity they would have if the printer did both of the conversions. As a result, link color conversion CMRs can improve system performance. The two types of link color conversion CMRs are: Link CMRs Link (LK) CMRs are unique. You cannot create a link CMR yourself and you do not include references to link CMRs in your print jobs. The print system creates and uses link CMRs automatically. If you use AFP Resource Installer, link CMRs are generated automatically when you create or install a color conversion CMR. As a result, your resource library always contains link CMRs for every combination of color conversion CMRs in audit (input) and instruction (output) processing modes. When link CMRs are created, AFP Resource Installer marks them as capturable, so the printer can save them to be used in other print jobs. If you do not use AFP Resource Installer, some printers can create link CMRs when they process print jobs. For example, if you send a print job to an InfoPrint 5000, the printer controller looks at the audit color conversion CMRs that are specified. Then, the print controller looks at the link CMRs that it has available to find one that combines the audit color conversion CMR with the appropriate instruction color conversion CMR. If it does not find one, the print controller creates the link CMR and uses it. The print controller can be configured to save the link CMRs that it creates. However, the link CMRs are sometimes removed during normal operation, for example, if the printer runs out of storage or is shut down. If the link is removed, the printer must create a new link CMR the next time it is needed. When a link CMR is created, the print system evaluates the conversion algorithms to and from the PCS. ## Code Page Mapping File for AFP Banner Pages

### File Location

The `banner_page_code_page_mapping.cfg` configuration file is stored in the following locations:

- **Linux (working copy):** `/aiw/aiw1/control_files/banner_pages/` [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
- **Linux (sample copy):** `/aiw/aiw1/samples/banner_pages/` [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
- **Windows (working copy):** `C:\aiw\aiw1\control_files\banner_pages\` [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
- **Windows (sample copy):** `C:\aiw\aiw1\samples\banner_pages\` [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ **Important:** It is recommended to make all changes in the `/aiw/aiw1/control_files/banner_pages/` copy, as updates may overwrite files in the `/aiw/aiw1/samples/banner_pages/` directory but will **not** overwrite files in the control_files directory. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Required Line Format

Each mapping line in the file must follow this exact format:

```
AFPCodedFontName=JavaCodePage
```

[aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]

- Lines beginning with a **`#`** (number sign) are treated as **comments**. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
- This format applies to both **SBCS** (Single-Byte Character Set) and **DBCS** (Double-Byte Character Set) coded fonts. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Steps to Add Mappings

1. Log in to the primary computer as the RICOH ProcessDirector system user (`aiw1` is the default). [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
2. Navigate to `/aiw/aiw1/control_files/banner_pages/`. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
3. Open `banner_page_code_page_mapping.cfg` with a text editor. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
4. Add your custom mappings in the user-defined section near the top of the file using the format `AFPCodedFontName=JavaCodePage`. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]
5. Save the configuration file. [aiw00bannerpcpm.pdf, Page 1]

# Comportement Normal après Modification d'un Code 39 dans AFP Editor

**Oui, c'est tout à fait normal.** Ce comportement est documenté et attendu.

## Explication

Après avoir cliqué sur **OK** dans la fenêtre de modification d'un Code 39, AFP Editor n'affiche **pas** le symbole de code-barres graphique dans le fichier AFP. À la place, vous verrez :

> **Une boîte (rectangle) entourant la zone du code-barres, avec le titre de la zone de code-barres affiché dans l'orientation que vous avez sélectionnée pour le symbole du code-barres.**

[modifyingbarcodes.pdf, Page 1]

## Pourquoi ce comportement ?

Ce comportement s'applique spécifiquement aux types de codes-barres suivants :

- **Code 39**
- Data Matrix
- Interleaved 2-of-5
- PDF417

Ces types affichent uniquement une boîte représentative, et **non** le symbole réel du code-barres dans l'éditeur visuel. [modifyingbarcodes.pdf, Page 1]

## Comparaison avec d'autres types de codes-barres

En revanche, les types suivants affichent bien le symbole réel du code-barres dans le fichier AFP :

| Type de code-barres | Affichage dans AFP Editor |
|---|---|
| IMB (Intelligent Mail) | ✅ Symbole réel affiché |
| POSTNET | ✅ Symbole réel affiché |
| QR Code | ✅ Symbole réel affiché |
| **Code 39** | ⬜ **Boîte uniquement** |
| Data Matrix | ⬜ Boîte uniquement |
| Interleaved 2-of-5 | ⬜ Boîte uniquement |
| PDF417 | ⬜ Boîte uniquement |

[modifyingbarcodes.pdf, Page 1] [creatingbarcodes.pdf, Page 1]

## En résumé

Il n'y a **aucun problème** avec votre fichier ou votre configuration. La boîte que vous voyez est la représentation visuelle normale d'un Code 39 dans RICOH Visual Workbench AFP Editor. Le code-barres sera correctement généré lors de l'impression. [modifyingbarcodes.pdf, Page 1]

If those resources are sent inline with the job, RICOH ProcessDirector uses the inline resources. If they are not inline, RICOH ProcessDirector must know where to find them on your system to be able to display, print, or convert the job correctly. Two kinds of resource libraries exist: those that use a resource access table (RAT) and those that do not use a RAT. A resource access table is an index of a resource library. The index is stored as a file in the library that it refers to. Color Management Resources (CMRs) and data objects must be stored in resource libraries that use a RAT. Other resources, such as form definitions, page definitions, and overlays, can be stored in resource libraries that do not use a RAT. You can configure RICOH ProcessDirector to use resources that are stored on any system in your network, as long as RICOH ProcessDirector can access the system that they reside on. However, it is recommended that you move all your resources to the default resource directory on your RICOH ProcessDirector primary computer. By storing them in that directory, all the RICOH ProcessDirector components, including any application/secondary servers that you install on different computers, can find them with no additional configuration. ## Placement of AFP Resources for Download for z/OS on a Linux System

When setting up Download for z/OS, AFP resources such as fonts and overlays should be placed in the **default resource directory** so that all components of RICOH ProcessDirector can access them without additional configuration.

---

### Recommended Location

Place your AFP resources in the following default resource directory on the Linux primary computer:

> **`/aiw/aiw1/resources`**

By storing resources in this directory, all RICOH ProcessDirector components — including any application/secondary servers installed on different computers — can find them with **no additional configuration** required. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

1. **Create any subdirectories** you want to use under `/aiw/aiw1/resources` to organize your AFP resources (e.g., fonts, overlays, page segments). [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Transfer the resource files** using an FTP client to move the resources into those subdirectories. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Important:** Make sure you transfer the files as **binary data**, not as text. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why This Directory?

- RICOH ProcessDirector **does not make any changes** to the `/aiw/aiw1/resources` directory during updates, so you do **not** need to reload the resources when installing an update. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]
- When a component needs a resource, RICOH ProcessDirector searches for it in the following order:
  1. Inline in the job
  2. Paths listed in the **AFP resource path** property of the job
  3. Paths listed in the **AFP resource path** property of the printer
  4. The default directory **`/aiw/aiw1/resources`** or `/usr/lpp/psf/reslib` [aiw00c9.pdf, Page 1]

---

### If Resources Cannot Be Moved to the Primary Computer

If you are unable to move resources to the primary computer, you can **NFS-mount** a directory from the remote computer onto your primary Linux computer. This requires installing NFS server and client software. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Additional Note on File Extensions (Linux)

Be aware that on Linux, **file extensions are case-sensitive** and **must be in uppercase**. [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]

## Configuring Mapped Drive Access for Inserter Controller on Windows RPD

Based on the provided documentation, here is the complete answer to your question:

---

### Which machine should the shared drive be set up from?

When RICOH ProcessDirector (RPD) is installed on a **Windows** primary server, the shared drive must be **set up from the inserter controller** — not from the primary server itself. [ConfiguringMappedDrives.pdf, Page 1]

> This is an important distinction: the setup originates on the **inserter controller's machine**, not on the RPD Windows server.

---

### Which file do you edit to ensure the mapped drive reconnects every time RPD starts?

You must edit the following file on the RPD Windows primary server:

```
C:\aiw\aiw1\bin\mountDrives.bat
```

This BAT file ensures that the mapped network drive is **mounted automatically whenever RICOH ProcessDirector starts**. [ConfiguringMappedDrives.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary of Steps (Windows Primary Server Scenario)

1. **Set up the shared drive from the inserter controller** (not from the RPD primary server). [ConfiguringMappedDrives.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Edit** `C:\aiw\aiw1\bin\mountDrives.bat` to include the drive mapping, so it reconnects each time RPD starts. [ConfiguringMappedDrives.pdf, Page 1]
3. For detailed guidance on creating and editing the BAT file, refer to the topic about mapping network drives in the RICOH ProcessDirector information center. [ConfiguringMappedDrives.pdf, Page 1]

## Testing REST API Calls in RICOH ProcessDirector Interactive Docs

Yes — actions performed through the REST API testing interface **do affect the live system**. Here is what you need to know:

---

### What Happens When You Test API Calls

When you use the interactive REST API documentation interface to test web services, **you are accessing the RICOH ProcessDirector primary server directly**. This means:

- Actions such as **creating, deleting, and enabling objects** are **executed on the primary server** and are **reflected in the RICOH ProcessDirector user interface** [aiw_RESTAPI.pdf, Page 1].

These are not sandbox or simulated operations — they are **real, live changes** to your production environment.

---

### Recommendation

Because test actions have real consequences on the live system, **it is strongly suggested that you create objects specifically for testing purposes** rather than using existing production objects [aiw_RESTAPI.pdf, Page 1].

---

### How to Access the Testing Interface

To access the REST API interactive documentation:

1. Open a web browser and enter your RICOH ProcessDirector **host name or IP address**.
2. Add `/restapi/` to the end of the address (e.g., `http://hostname:15080/restapi/`) [aiw_RESTAPI.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Summary

| Action Tested via Interactive Docs | Impact on Live System |
|---|---|
| Creating objects | ✅ Yes — object is created on primary server |
| Deleting objects | ✅ Yes — object is deleted on primary server |
| Enabling objects | ✅ Yes — change is reflected in the UI |

## List Batching Method: File Not Matching Data Patterns

When using the **List batching method**, if a file listed in the list file does **not** match the **Data patterns** value on the input device, the following occurs:

> The input device **does not identify the file as a print file**. Because the listed print file appears to be missing, **the input device waits for it and does not create the job.**

[aiw_sdk_list.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Explanation in Context

The **Data patterns** property defines a pattern (regular expression) that must match the file names of your print files. By default, the value is `.*$`, which matches all file names. [aiw_sdk_list.pdf, Page 1]

Here is what happens step by step:

1. The input device receives a list file and reads the file names listed within it. [aiw_sdk_list.pdf, Page 1]
2. It then looks for each file listed in the list file. [aiw_sdk_list.pdf, Page 1]
3. If a listed file's name **does not match** the Data patterns value, the input device **fails to recognize it as a print file**. [aiw_sdk_list.pdf, Page 1]
4. Since the file appears to be "missing" from the input device's perspective, **the input device waits indefinitely** and **does not submit or create the job**. [aiw_sdk_list.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Key Takeaway

Ensure that the **Data patterns** value is configured to correctly match the file names of all print files referenced in your list file. A mismatch will cause the job to be **stalled**, as the input device will keep waiting for a file it cannot recognize.

## Exporting a List of Objects and Their Properties from RICOH ProcessDirector

### Overview

RICOH ProcessDirector provides a built-in feature that allows you to compile and export a list of objects (such as printers, input devices, servers, etc.) along with their properties. [aiw00ao.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What Objects Can Be Exported?

The following types of objects are supported:
- **Servers**
- **Notifications**
- **Media**
- **Input devices**
- **Printers**
- Additional objects added by optional features [aiw00ao.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Output Format

When you export the entries from an object table, RICOH ProcessDirector produces a **Comma-Separated Values (CSV) file**. [aiw00ao.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Purpose / Use Cases

There are **two distinct export functions** worth distinguishing:

1. **Compiling a list of objects and their properties:**
   This exports the object table entries to a **CSV file**, which is useful for documentation or review purposes. [aiw00ao.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Reusing objects on another RICOH ProcessDirector system:**
   You can also export objects (e.g., input devices, printers) for **import onto another RICOH ProcessDirector system**. [aiw00ao.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Steps to Compile the List

Based on the available documentation, the process involves:

1. Navigate to the relevant **object table** in the RICOH ProcessDirector user interface (e.g., the Printers table).
2. Use the **export function** available within that table.
3. RICOH ProcessDirector will generate and provide a **CSV file** containing the objects and their associated properties. [aiw00ao.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Prerequisites for Assigning Image or Text Content to White Space Areas in AFP Files

Before you can start assigning image or text content to white space areas in AFP files, you must complete the following prerequisite step:

### You Must Create White Space Definitions First

You must create **one or more white space definitions** before you can assign content to white space areas. [assigningcontent.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How White Space Definitions Are Created

There are two methods available for defining white space in AFP files:

1. **Creating definitions for known white space** – Use this method when you know white space exists on the same page in all page groups. [addingwsafpfiles.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Creating definitions by searching for white space** – Use this method when you do not know where white space exists. Whitespace Manager will search for the largest white space area on a page that meets the minimum dimensions you specify. [addingwsafpfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Overall Workflow Summary

Once your white space definitions are in place, the general process is:

1. Open a sample AFP file and its control file in **RICOH Visual Workbench**. [insertingimages.pdf, Page 1]
2. Switch to **Whitespace Manager** mode via **Mode ⇒ Whitespace Manager**. [insertingimages.pdf, Page 1]
3. Use **Tools ⇒ Manage Campaigns** to create rules that determine what content is assigned and under what conditions. [assigningcontent.pdf, Page 1]

In short, **defining your white space areas is the essential prerequisite** before any content assignment can begin. [assigningcontent.pdf, Page 1]

## Two Step Templates for XML Manipulation in RICOH ProcessDirector

Based on the provided documentation, there are **two step templates** specifically designed to manipulate XML files in RICOH ProcessDirector:

---

### 1. 📄 `CreateJobsFromXML`

This step template **creates jobs from elements in an XML file that match an XPath expression**. Specifically, a step based on this template:

- Reads an XML file and identifies elements that match a specified XPath expression
- Creates individual jobs from those matching XML elements
- Submits the newly created jobs to a designated workflow
- Can be used **multiple times** within or across workflows, each with a different XPath expression to handle different levels of XML structure (e.g., first creating a job per order, then a job per item within each order)

[aiw_o_xml_JobsWith.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_c_xml_PrepToReceive.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_o_xml_scen_orders.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. 🔄 `ApplyXSLTransform`

This step template **transforms XML into other formats**. Specifically, a step based on this template:

- Transforms XML into a file that **specifies the values of RICOH ProcessDirector job or document properties**
- Transforms XML into **another XML format**
- Can also be used to **assign a URL** (found within an XML element) to the value of a job property, enabling a subsequent step based on the `DownloadFile` step template to download that file

[aiw_o_xml_JobsWith.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_c_xml_PrepToReceive.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 📝 Summary Table

| Step Template | Primary Function |
|---|---|
| `CreateJobsFromXML` | Creates jobs from XML elements matching an XPath expression and submits them to a workflow |
| `ApplyXSLTransform` | Transforms XML into property value files or another XML format using XSLT style sheets |

> **Note:** You can also use steps based on other step templates, such as `RunExternalProgram`, to manipulate XML files, but these two are the ones **specifically designed** for XML manipulation. [aiw_c_xml_PrepToReceive.pdf, Page 1]

## Making an Inserter Controller Change Take Effect for an Existing Job

If you change the **Inserter controller** property for a job that is already in the system, you need to take the following action:

---

### Required Action: Use the "Process Again" Action

Use the **Process Again** action to reprocess the job, starting at the appropriate step:

- Start reprocessing from the step based on the **WriteInserterControlFile** step template *(if one exists in the workflow)*, **OR**
- Start reprocessing from the step based on the **InsertJobs** step template.

[AssociatingInserterControllersWithJobs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why This Is Necessary

RICOH ProcessDirector uses the inserter controller object associated with a job to:

1. **Write** the inserter control file for the job and send it to the inserter controller.
2. **Receive** the inserter results file from the inserter controller and interpret it.

[AssociatingInserterControllersWithJobs.pdf, Page 1]

Simply changing the property alone is not sufficient — the job must be reprocessed from the correct step so that the updated inserter controller object is actually applied to the job's control file generation and results handling.

## AFP Editor: Correcting an Incorrect Page Number for Hidden Area Placement

When setting the placement of a hidden area to a specific page number ("Page n") in AFP Editor, you **cannot change the page number directly**. The page number is determined by the page on which you originally drew the box for the hidden area.

### What to do if the page number is wrong:

Follow these steps:

1. **Click Cancel** on the current window (whether you are in the process of creating or modifying the hidden area). [hidingareas.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Navigate to the correct page** in the AFP file where you want the hidden area to be placed.
3. **Draw the box for the hidden area again** on the correct page. [hidingareas.pdf, Page 1]

This applies both when **creating** a new hidden area and when **modifying** an existing one. As stated for the Modify Hidden Area window:

> *"You cannot change this page number. If the page number is incorrect, click Cancel and draw the box for the hidden area on the correct page."* [modfiyinghiddenareas.pdf, Page 1]

### Summary

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Page number is wrong | Click **Cancel** |
| After cancelling | Go to the **correct page** and **redraw** the hidden area box |

There is no way to manually type or edit the "Page n" value — it is always set automatically based on where you draw the box. [hidingareas.pdf, Page 1] [modfiyinghiddenareas.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## RICOH Visual Workbench AFP Indexer – Text Block Index Tags

### 1. Can you add more characters to the text value than what's already in the block?

**No.** You can only *reduce* the number of characters used for the index value — you **cannot increase** the characters in a text block. Specifically, you may edit the text block to remove unwanted characters (such as blanks or special characters), but adding characters beyond what exists in the block is not permitted. [creatingindexes.pdf, Page 1]

This same restriction applies when creating page-level indexes as well: *"You can edit the text block to reduce the number of characters you use for the index value (you cannot increase the characters in a text block)."* [definingpageswithindex.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. What is the range for the Position Threshold on the Advanced tab?

The threshold range depends on your chosen measurement unit:

| Measurement Unit | Minimum | Maximum |
|-----------------|---------|---------|
| **Inches** | 1/100 inch | 1 inch |
| **Millimeters** | 1 mm | 25 mm |

[creatingindexes.pdf, Page 1]

#### Additional details about the threshold:
- The threshold defines **how far the text can be from its original location** and still be considered a match for the index tag — either vertically or horizontally. [creatingindexes.pdf, Page 1]
- The **default threshold value** is **10** (for inches) or **2** (for millimeters), which is usually sufficient. [creatingindexes.pdf, Page 1]
- ⚠️ **Caution:** If you increase the threshold above the default, you may create an unexpected index tag, because matching is done **only on location** — the first text block found within the threshold range will be used as the index tag. [creatingindexes.pdf, Page 1]

## Banner Pages: AFP vs PDF in RICOH ProcessDirector

### AFP Banner Pages

AFP print jobs support **three types** of banner pages [aiw_bannerpages.pdf, Page 1]:

1. **Header pages** – print **before** the first data pages of a job [aiw_afpbanners.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Trailer pages** – print **after** the last data pages of a job [aiw_afpbanners.pdf, Page 1]
3. **Separator pages** – print **between copies** of a multi-copy job [aiw_afpbanners.pdf, Page 1]

AFP banner pages can be used **in any combination** with AFP print jobs printed to AFP printer objects [aiw_bannerpages.pdf, Page 1].

> **Note:** For header and trailer pages to print, the **Header copies** and **Trailer copies** job properties must be set to **1 or greater**. If set to 0, those banner pages will not print even if enabled on the printer [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1].

---

### PDF Banner Pages

PDF print jobs support **two types** of banner pages [aiw_bannerpages.pdf, Page 1]:

1. **Header pages** – print **before** the first data pages of a job [aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Trailer pages** – print **after** the last data pages of a job [aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1]

> **Important:** PDF banner pages do **not** support separator pages between copies. This is a key difference from AFP.

PDF banner pages can also be used with jobs in **other data streams**, but only if the destination printer supports printing PDF files [aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1].

> **Note:** If a PDF 2.0 file is printed with banner pages, it will be **converted to PDF 1.7 format**, which is required for banner page support [aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Summary of Differences

| Feature | AFP Jobs | PDF Jobs |
|---|---|---|
| Header pages | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| Trailer pages | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| Separator pages (between copies) | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Other data streams supported | ❌ AFP printers only | ✅ Yes (if printer supports PDF) |

## Step Templates That Must Run on Application Servers (Linux Primary Server)

When the RICOH ProcessDirector primary computer is a **Linux system**, the following step templates (and any copies of them) **must be tuned to run on application servers** [aiwtunesteptemplate.pdf, Page 1]:

|---|

| **RunFusionPro** |
| **RunImpostripOnJob** |

Follow these steps to configure them to run on application servers [aiwtunesteptemplate.pdf, Page 1]:

1. Click the **Workflow** tab.
2. In the left pane, click **Step Templates**.
3. Click the **name** of the step template you want to tune.
4. Click the **Tuning** tab.
5. In the **Servers to use** section, specify that steps based on this step template run on the appropriate **application servers** (restricted to selected servers, not the general pool).

## Placement of the EmailDocuments Step in a Workflow

Based on the official RICOH ProcessDirector documentation, here is the precise guidance on where to place the **EmailDocuments** step relative to **PreparePDFOutputForFinishing** and **BuildPDFFromDocuments**:

---

### Core Rule

The **EmailDocuments** step must be placed:
- **After** the `BuildPDFFromDocuments` step
- **Before** any step that reorders documents at the **job level**, such as `PreparePDFOutputForFinishing` or `ReversePDFPageOrder`

[doc_c_emailingdocs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Typical Step Order (Print + Email Workflow)

For jobs that both **email and print** documents, the recommended step order is:

1. `IdentifyPDFDocuments`
2. `SortDocuments`
3. `BuildPDFFromDocuments`
4. **`EmailDocuments`** ← placed here
5. `PreparePDFOutputForFinishing`
6. `PrintJobs`

[doc_c_emailingdocs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Alternative: Using a SnapshotJobFile Step

If you need to keep a copy of the job file in the spool directory for email extraction, you can place a `SnapshotJobFile` step **after** `BuildPDFFromDocuments` and **before** the job-level reordering step. In this case, `EmailDocuments` can be placed **after** `PreparePDFOutputForFinishing`:

1. `IdentifyPDFDocuments`
2. `SortDocuments`
3. `BuildPDFFromDocuments`
4. `SnapshotJobFile`
5. `PreparePDFOutputForFinishing`
6. `PrintJobs`
7. **`EmailDocuments`** ← placed here (using the snapshot file)

[doc_c_emailingdocs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Important Notes

- The `EmailDocuments` step **can** be placed after steps that reorder documents at the **document level** (e.g., `GroupDocuments`, `SortDocuments`, `SplitDocuments`), as these do not conflict with email processing. [doc_c_emailingdocs.pdf, Page 1]

A typical branching setup connects `BuildPDFFromDocuments` to both the `EmailDocuments` step and the print path, with rules such as `Custom 1 = Email` on the connector leading to `EmailDocuments`. [pref_o_scen_distribute.pdf, Page 2]

# Job-Level Settings to Check When AFP Banner Pages Don't Print

Even when header and trailer pages are enabled at the AFP printer level, certain **job-level properties** can prevent them from printing. Here is what you need to check:

---

## ✅ Primary Setting to Check: Header Copies and Trailer Copies

The most critical job-level settings are the **Header copies** and **Trailer copies** properties on the individual job.

> **For header and trailer pages to print, the values for the Header copies and Trailer copies properties for the job must be set to 1 or greater. If the values for those job properties are set to 0, the printer does not print a header page or a trailer page for a specific job, even though these types [of banner pages are enabled on the printer].** [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1]

### Step-by-Step Check:

1. Locate the affected job in RICOH ProcessDirector.
2. Open the job's properties.
3. Check the **Header copies** property — ensure it is set to **1 or greater** (not 0). [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1]
4. Check the **Trailer copies** property — ensure it is also set to **1 or greater** (not 0). [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1]
5. If either value is **0**, update it to **1** (or the desired number of copies) and resubmit or reprint the job.

---

## 📋 Summary Table

| Job Property | Required Value | Effect if Set to 0 |
|---|---|---|
| **Header copies** | ≥ 1 | Header page will NOT print [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1] |
| **Trailer copies** | ≥ 1 | Trailer page will NOT print [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1] |

---

## Additional Note: Banner Page Appearance (Control File)

If the pages print but do not look correct, note that each job must also specify what the banner page should look like via a **control file**. The control file may be set by the workflow, but can be changed for an individual job after it enters the system. [aiw_afpbanners.pdf, Page 1]

---

**In summary:** The printer-level enable settings alone are not sufficient — the job's own **Header copies** and **Trailer copies** properties must each be set to **1 or greater**, otherwise the printer will skip banner pages for that specific job regardless of printer configuration. [aiw00c6.pdf, Page 1]

OK The job is on schedule to meet the next planned checkpoint. However, it could have missed a previous checkpoint. When the checkpoint status for a job is Late, RICOH ProcessDirector adds a yellow dot in the Deadlines portlet and in the Schedule risk column for the job in the Jobs table. In addition, RICOH ProcessDirector can display the checkpoint status as a column in the Jobs table so the operator can use the Filter function to display jobs with a value of Late for the Checkpoint status property. After a job is removed from the system, the audit file for the job (jobnumber.yy-mm-dd_hh-mm-ss.policy_properties.cfg.csv) can contain the final checkpoint status. Parent topic: Service policies


Answer:

## Expected Work Monitoring: Input Device Status When Jobs Are Late

When setting up expected work monitoring in RICOH ProcessDirector, here is what happens if some jobs haven't arrived by the scheduled check time:

---

### What Happens at the Scheduled Check Time

At the configured check time, the input device automatically evaluates how many jobs have arrived. There are two possible outcomes:

1. **All expected jobs have arrived** → Processing continues as usual with no alerts. [dt_o_scen_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]

2. **One or more jobs have NOT arrived** → The following occurs:
   - The **"Expected work status" property** of the input device is set to **"Late"**. [dt_o_scen_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1]
   - An **alert (⚠) icon appears to the right of the input device** in the interface, making it visually prominent for operators. [dt_o_scen_expectedwork.pdf, Page 1] [dt_o_featov.pdf, Page 3]

---

### Operator Response

Once the alert icon appears, **the operator can respond by tracking down the missing jobs** to investigate why they have not arrived. [dt_o_featov.pdf, Page 3]

---

### Optional Notification

You can also set up a **notification object to send an email** when expected work for an input device is late, so that the right people are alerted automatically without needing to monitor the interface manually. [sla_settingupexpwork.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Scenario | Input Device Status | Visual Indicator |
|---|---|---|
| All jobs arrived on time | Normal | No alert |
| One or more jobs missing | **Late** | ⚠ Alert icon appears |

1. Click the **Administration** tab. [slausingsuppliednoservice.pdf, Page 1]
2. In the left pane, click **Objects ⇒ No-Service Periods**. [slausingsuppliednoservice.pdf, Page 1]

# Ways to Make an External Preferences File Available to RICOH ProcessDirector

There are **three main methods** you can use to make an external preferences file available to RICOH ProcessDirector [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]:

---

## Method 1: Submit the Preferences File Together with the Job

You can submit a job and a preferences file **together to an input device** at the same time.

**Required configuration steps:**

1. Select the input device on the Input Devices portlet [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
2. If the input device is enabled, disable it [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
3. Click **Actions ⇒ Properties** [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
4. Click the **Batching tab** and set the **Batching method** property to **Pattern** [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
5. Configure a file pattern to identify the **job file** (e.g., for PDF jobs):
   - File pattern: `.*pdf$`
   - Spool file usage: `print`
   - Spool file type: `pdf`
   - File pattern required: `Yes`
   - File pattern sequence: `1` [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
6. Click **Add**, then configure a second file pattern to identify the **preferences file** (e.g., for CSV format):
   - File pattern: `.*csv$`
   - Spool file usage: `pref`
   - Spool file type: `csv`
   - File pattern required: `Yes`
   - File pattern sequence: `2` [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
7. In the workflow's **ApplyPreferences** step, set the **Preferences file** property to the symbolic name of the file, for example:
   `${getFileName(pref,csv,read)}` [pref_c_createworkflow.pdf, Page 1]

> **Note:** If the preferences file is tab-delimited with a `.txt` extension, change the File pattern and Spool file type values to `.*txt$` and `txt` respectively [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Method 2: Store the Preferences File in a Static Location on the Primary Computer

You can **copy a preferences file to a directory on the primary computer** for use with multiple jobs.

**Required configuration steps:**

- No special input device batching configuration is needed for this method — you only need to configure the **ApplyPreferences step** to find the preferences file [pref_c_SendPrefFileToSystem.pdf, Page 1]
- In the workflow's **ApplyPreferences** step, set the **Preferences file** property to the full path and name of the file, for example:
  `/aiw/aiw1/preferences/preferences.csv` [pref_c_createworkflow.pdf, Page 1]

## Service Policies for Three SLA Commitments

### How Many Service Policies Do You Need?

You will need to set up **three service policies** — one for each SLA commitment.

> "Each service policy defines job checkpoints and an SLA that apply to one specific performance commitment. For example, if an installation has **three performance commitments** for different types of jobs or for different clients, the administrator would **create three service policies**." [slapolicy.pdf, Page 1]

This is also confirmed by the general guidance that you can create a service policy for each performance commitment:

> "You can create a service policy for each performance commitment. For example, you can create one service policy for jobs that need to be printed in 1 day, and another service policy for jobs that need to be printed in 2 days." [slacreatingpolicies.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How Are Service Policies Applied to Jobs?

Service policies are applied to jobs **through workflows**. Here is how it works step by step:

1. **Create your three service policies** via Administration → Objects → Service Policies → Add. [slacreatingpolicies.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Associate each service policy with one or more workflows.** Each workflow can have only **one** associated service policy. [slaassociatingwithjobtype2.pdf, Page 1]

3. **As each job arrives**, RICOH ProcessDirector automatically uses the service policy associated with that job's workflow to set checkpoints and a deadline for the job:
   > "As each job arrives in the system, RICOH ProcessDirector uses the service policy that is associated with the workflow to set checkpoints and a deadline for the job." [slapolicy.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Handling Multiple Clients Using the Same Workflow

If two or more of your client types currently share the same workflow, you will need to **create separate workflows** for each — one per service policy:

> "If more than one service policy applies to a workflow, you might need to create additional workflows. For example, if you have created two service policies – one for jobs from client ABC and another for jobs from client XYZ – and both clients use workflow PDF, you could create another PDF workflow. The workflows can have identical properties except for the associated service policy. You might, for example, name the two workflows **PDF.ABC** and **PDF.XYZ**." [slaassociatingwithjobtype.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Client Type | Service Policy | Workflow |
|---|---|---|
| Client Type 1 | Service Policy A | Workflow.Client1 |
| Client Type 2 | Service Policy B | Workflow.Client2 |
| Client Type 3 | Service Policy C | Workflow.Client3 |

In short: **3 SLA commitments = 3 service policies**, each linked to its own dedicated workflow so that jobs are automatically tracked against the correct SLA upon arrival. [slapolicy.pdf, Page 1] [slasettinguppolicies.pdf, Page 1]

## Setting Up Japanese DBCS Fonts for AFP Banner Pages

Here are the step-by-step instructions for copying the font files and editing the configuration file:

---

### Step 1 – Install the Required Font CDs on the Primary Computer

First, install fonts from these two CDs on the primary computer [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1]:

- **AFP Outline Fonts (LCD4-5683)** – usable on Linux and Windows; includes Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese fonts.
- **WorldType Fonts (LCD4-5684)** – OpenType and TrueType fonts in Microsoft Unicode format.

---

### Step 2 – Log In as the System User

Log in to the primary computer as the RICOH ProcessDirector system user (**`aiw1`** is the default) [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Step 3 – Locate the Font Files

In the documentation for the fonts you installed, find the installation location of the Japanese DBCS-coded font(s) you want to use (for example, **`XZAE26F`**) [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Step 4 – Copy the Font Files to the Primary Server

Copy the DBCS-coded fonts to the following directory on the RICOH ProcessDirector **primary computer** from which you will print banner pages with Japanese characters [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1]:

```
/usr/lpp/psf/reslib
```

---

### Step 5 – Edit the Configuration File to Map Fonts to Java Code Pages

1. Navigate to the following directory [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1]:
   ```
   /aiw/aiw1/control_files/banner_pages/
   ```

2. Open the following configuration file with a text editor [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1]:
   ```
   banner_page_code_page_mapping.cfg
   ```

3. Map the copied coded fonts to their corresponding **Java code pages**. Most Japanese DBCS-coded fonts map to the **IBM930** or **IBM939** code page. For example, add a line such as [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1]:
   ```
   XZE26F=IBM939
   ```

4. **Save** the configuration file [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Additional Note

> ⚠️ The printer that prints the banner pages **must support DBCS characters** [aiw00bannerjfont.pdf, Page 1].

A sample `banner_page_code_page_mapping.cfg` file is also available for reference at `/aiw/aiw1/samples/banner_pages/` [aiw_afpbanners.pdf, Page 1].

## Setting the Starting Position When a Scanner Reads Only a Subset of Barcode Characters

When your barcode scanner is configured to read only a portion of the full barcode (a subset of characters), you need to adjust the starting position in the barcode format to account for this. Here is how to set it correctly:

---

### Key Rule

**The barcode format must match how the camera or barcode scanner hardware is configured.** [CreatingBarCodeFormats.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Set the Starting Position

If the scanner is reading only a subset of characters from the barcode, you should **set the starting position to 1**, regardless of where that property actually begins in the full barcode. [BarCodeFormatObject.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Example

Consider this scenario:
- A document property value starts at **position 10** in the full barcode.
- The barcode scanner is configured to read **only characters 10 through 25**.

In this case:
1. Navigate to **Administration → Objects → Barcode Formats**. [CreatingBarCodeFormats.pdf, Page 1]
2. Add or edit the relevant property in the barcode format.
3. In the **Property start** field, specify **position 1** — because from the scanner's perspective, the first character it reads (character 10 of the full barcode) is effectively position 1. [CreatingBarCodeFormats.pdf, Page 1]
4. In the **Property length** field, specify the length of the property value as normal. [CreatingBarCodeFormats.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Scenario | Full Barcode Position | Scanner Reads | Set Property Start To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scanner reads full barcode | Position 10 | All characters | **10** |
| Scanner reads only chars 10–25 | Position 10 | Characters 10–25 only | **1** |

> *"If the barcode scanner is configured to read the value of only one property in the barcode, specify that this value starts in position 1 of the barcode."* [CreatingBarCodeFormats.pdf, Page 1]

## Checkpoint Times After Removing a No-Service Period

**No, checkpoint times do NOT automatically update.**

When you delete or remove a no-service period, the checkpoint times and deadlines for jobs already in the system remain unchanged — even if those times were originally calculated using that no-service period. [slapolicynoservice.pdf, Page 1] [slanoservice.pdf, Page 1]

---

### To Reset the Checkpoint Times

If you need the checkpoint times to reflect the removal of the no-service period, you must **manually reprocess the job from the beginning**. Here is what to do:

1. Locate the affected job(s) in RICOH ProcessDirector.
2. Use the **Process Again** action to reprocess the job from the **first step**.
3. RICOH ProcessDirector will then recalculate new **planned checkpoint times**, taking into account any changes to the service policy or no-service periods. [slapolicycheckpointtimes.pdf, Page 1]

## Re-enabling the Autostart Script for RICOH ProcessDirector on Linux

To reactivate the autostart script for a RICOH ProcessDirector primary or secondary server, follow these steps:

---

### Prerequisites / Important Notes

> **Note:** You only need to perform these steps if you previously deactivated the autostart script. When RICOH ProcessDirector is installed, the autostart script is **active by default**. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]

> You will also need the **`n` and `nn` numbers** that you noted when you originally deactivated the script, as these determine when the script runs. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Steps to Re-enable the Autostart Script

**Step 1:** Log in as the **root user**. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 2:** Access the **command line**. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 3:** Add two symbolic links to reactivate the script by entering the following commands: [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]

```bash
ln -s /etc/init.d/aiwserv /etc/init.d/rcn.d/Snnaiwserv
ln -s /etc/init.d/aiwserv /etc/init.d/rcn.d/Knnaiwserv
```

> Replace **`n`** and **`nn`** with the numbers you recorded when you deactivated the autostart script. These numbers control the order in which the script runs at startup. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Result

Once these symbolic links are in place, RICOH ProcessDirector (base product or secondary server) will **start automatically whenever the system starts**. [aiw00a38.pdf, Page 1]
