## Using "Last Page" Instead of "This Page" for Variable-Length Page Groups

When page groups have a variable number of pages and you need white space to always appear on the final page, you should use the **"Last page"** option instead of "This page".

---

### Why Use "Last Page"?

The documentation explicitly states:

> *"You might want to create a Last page definition instead of This page when the page groups contain a variable number of pages and you want the white space to always be on the last page."*

[creatingwsdefavail.pdf, Page 1] [creatingwsdefsearch.pdf, Page 1] [whitespace_overview.pdf, Page 1] [whitespace_overview.pdf, Page 2]

---

### How "Last Page" Works

- **For known white space:** Whitespace Manager creates a white space definition on the last page of the page group and displays it as a colored box. If a white space definition was previously found on the page from a search, the known white space definition takes precedence. [whitespace_overview.pdf, Page 1]

- **For white space from a search:** Whitespace Manager creates a white space definition on the last page of the page group and displays it as a colored box, **unless** a known white space area is already defined on the page, or no white space area meets the specified dimensions. [whitespace_overview.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Important Constraint

⚠️ You can **only select the "Last page" option if the current page is the last page in the page group**. If the option is grayed out, it is unavailable from your current position in the document. [creatingwsdefavail.pdf, Page 1] [creatingwsdefsearch.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Scenario | Recommended Option |
|---|---|
| White space always on a **fixed** page | **This page** |
| White space always on the **final page** of variable-length page groups | **Last page** ✅ |

# Four Ways to Create Index Tags in an AFP File Using RICOH ProcessDirector

According to the documentation, you can create index tags in AFP files using the AFP Indexer mode of RICOH Visual Workbench in the following **four ways**:

---

## 1. 📝 Index Tags for Text Blocks
You can create an index tag for a **block of text** that occurs in a consistent location on the same page in every page group, on a supplemental page, or on an individual page in a page group. For example, you can create an index tag for a block of text that contains a customer name or an account number. You can also edit the text value to remove unwanted text such as blanks or special characters. [indextags_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 2. 📐 Index Tags in Areas (Index Areas)
You can create an **index area** that occurs in a consistent location on the same page in every page group or supplemental page, and then create index tags within that area. Within an index area, you can create index tags that **span multiple text blocks** on the same line — for example, concatenating the first and second halves of an account number into a single index tag. [indextags_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 3. 📬 Index Tags for Address Areas
You can create index tags for an **address area** in a page group or supplemental page. This is particularly useful when mailing addresses contain a **different number of lines** in each page group (e.g., one document may have four address lines while another has five). Within an address area, you can perform specialized functions such as creating an index tag for a ZIP Code in U.S. Postal Service format. [indextags_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 4. 🔧 Index Tags from NOP Records
You can create index tags from **No Operation (NOP) records**. A NOP record causes an application to move to the next instruction without taking any other action. NOP records can be found anywhere in a page group and are **not viewable or printable**, but the data contained within them can be used to create index tags. [indextags_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

> These four methods are also reflected in the section structure of the Creating Index Tags documentation, which lists: *Creating index tags for text blocks*, *Creating index tags in areas*, *Creating index tags in address areas*, and *Creating index tags from NOP records*. [creatingindexescontainer.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Why You Can't Copy CMR Files Directly into an AFP Resource Library

This is an excellent question, and the reason comes down to how AFP resource libraries that contain CMRs are **indexed and accessed** by the print server.

---

### The Core Issue: The Resource Access Table (RAT)

Resource libraries used for CMRs rely on a **Resource Access Table (RAT)** as their index. The RAT is a file stored inside the library that acts as a catalogue of all the resources contained within it. When a print server needs to locate a CMR, it **first consults the RAT** — it does not simply scan the directory for files. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What Happens When You Copy a CMR Directly?

If you copy a CMR file directly into the resource library folder (bypassing AFP Resource Installer), **the RAT is never updated**. Because the print server relies entirely on the RAT to find resources, it will be unable to locate the CMR you copied in — even though the file physically exists in the directory. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

> *"If you copy CMRs or data objects into these resource libraries, the RAT is not updated so the print server cannot use it to find the CMRs or data objects."* [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why Overlays and Form Definitions Are Different

Other AFP resources such as **overlays, form definitions, and page definitions** can be stored in resource libraries that do **not** use a RAT. This is why you can copy those files directly into a directory and have them work without any additional steps. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

CMRs (and data objects), however, **must** be stored in RAT-based libraries, which means they require the proper tooling to be installed correctly. [aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1]

---

### The Correct Approach

You must **always use AFP Resource Installer** to manage CMRs in your resource libraries. Specifically, AFP Resource Installer must be used to: [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

1. **Add** CMRs and data objects to a resource library (so the RAT is updated).
2. **Modify** properties of CMRs and data objects listed in the RAT.
3. **Update** an existing CMR — do not replace it by copying a new version directly into the library.
4. **Move or replicate** CMRs to a different resource library location.

> ⚠️ You should also **never directly edit the RAT** or any files within the resource library manually. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Resource Type | Requires RAT-based Library | Can Copy Directly? |
|---|---|---|
| CMRs | ✅ Yes | ❌ No — use AFP Resource Installer |
| Data Objects | ✅ Yes (recommended) | ❌ No — use AFP Resource Installer |
| Overlays, Form Definitions, Page Definitions | ❌ Not required | ✅ Yes |

[aiwcafpres.pdf, Page 1] [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Which File Gets Sent to the Kodak PDF Printer When Both Formats Exist?

When a job has **both PostScript and PDF versions** in the spool directory, the determining rule is straightforward:

> **The file with the most recent timestamp is sent to the printer.**

Specifically:

1. **If both formats exist** in the job's spool directory at the time the job is scheduled for printing, RICOH ProcessDirector will send whichever file has the **most recent modification time** to the Kodak PDF printer. [kdk_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

2. **A common scenario** that illustrates this rule: if a transform converts a PostScript file to PDF, the resulting **PDF format of the file is sent** to the Kodak PDF printer — because the newly converted PDF will have a more recent timestamp than the original PostScript file. [kdk_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

### Summary Table

| Situation | File Sent to Printer |
|---|---|
| Both PS and PDF exist; PDF is newer | PDF file |
| Both PS and PDF exist; PS is newer | PostScript file |
| Transform converts PS → PDF | PDF file (most recent) |

> 💡 **Key takeaway:** It is **not** automatically always the PDF — it is always the **most recently timestamped** file of the two formats available in the spool directory at scheduling time. [kdk_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

## Remove All Displayed Notes in RICOH ProcessDirector

When you use **"Remove all displayed notes"**, it only deletes the notes that are **currently visible in the Notes panel** — not every note in the entire system.

### How it works:

1. Click the **three dots** at the top of the Notes panel.
2. Select **"Remove all displayed notes"**.
3. On the confirmation dialog, click **OK**. [create_edit_notes.pdf, Page 1]

### Important clarification:

> **Only the notes currently visible in the Notes panel are deleted.** [create_edit_notes.pdf, Page 1]

This means that if you have applied a filter (for example, filtering by a specific user mention or object), only the notes matching that filter — and therefore currently displayed — will be removed. Notes that are not currently shown in the panel will **not** be affected.

### Additional points to be aware of:

- You **cannot manually select multiple individual notes** for selective deletion; the "Remove all displayed notes" action removes **all visible notes at once**. [create_edit_notes.pdf, Page 1]
- RICOH ProcessDirector **creates a record** of the removed notes in the **audit files**. [create_edit_notes.pdf, Page 1]
- Separately from manual removal, notes are also **automatically deleted after a predefined expiration period** to keep the system clean and relevant. [create_edit_notes.pdf, Page 1]

### In summary:
| Action | Scope |
|---|---|
| Remove all displayed notes | Only notes **currently visible** in the panel |
| System-wide deletion | **Not possible** via this action |

## Splitting an AFP Job by Document Property

Based on the provided documentation, here is a complete answer to your question:

### Step Template to Use

Instead of using the **SplitDocuments** step template, you should use a step based on the **GroupDocuments** step template. Each group of documents then becomes a separate child job. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

### Number of Grouping Criteria

You can apply **up to six (6) grouping criteria** to create child jobs. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

For example, each child job could contain all statements for each of five cities in each of 10 countries — demonstrating how multiple criteria can be combined. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

---

The recommended parent workflow steps are as follows: [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

| Phase | Step |
|---|---|
| **Receive** | SetJobPropsFromTextFile *(Input data stream: AFP)* |
| **Prepare** | UseInlineFormDefinition → IndexAFP → EnableRepositioning → IdentifyDocuments |
| **Assemble** | **GroupDocuments** → CreateJobsFromDocuments |
| **Complete** | RetainCompletedJobs → RemoveJobs |

The child workflow then handles building and printing the AFP output via steps such as **BuildAFPFromDocuments**, **EnableRepositioning**, **CreatePageRanges**, and **PrintJobs**. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

## Bank Statement Reprint Scenario: StoreInRepository Placement and Configuration

### Why StoreInRepository is Placed BEFORE RetainCompletedJobs

The **StoreInRepository step is placed after the PrintJobs step but before the RetainCompletedJobs step** for a specific and important reason: the job and its data need to be captured and saved to the repository **while the job is still active and complete with its print information**, before the RetainCompletedJobs step eventually deletes it from the Jobs table.

As described in the bank statement scenario: *"The administrator adds a step based on the StoreInRepository step template after the PrintJobs step in the PDF print workflow, but before the RetainCompletedJobs step, and saves the print file."* [rep_o_scen_ReprintDocument.pdf, Page 1]

The practical reason for this ordering is that the commercial printer only retains jobs for **three days** in the Jobs table. After those three days, the RetainCompletedJobs step causes the job to be deleted. By placing StoreInRepository **before** RetainCompletedJobs, the system ensures the job, its properties, and its history are safely archived in the repository **before** it disappears from the Jobs table. This allows reprints to be fulfilled for up to **four years** after the original print run [rep_o_scen_ReprintDocument.pdf, Page 1].

This approach also means the retention period in RetainCompletedJobs can be kept short (e.g., three days) without losing long-term access to job data, since the repository now serves as the long-term archive. As the planning documentation notes: *"You can reduce the retention period because now you can reprint from the repository."* [rep_c_PlanForRetention.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Job and Document Properties Configured to be Stored

In the bank statement reprint scenario, the administrator configures the following properties in the StoreInRepository step:

#### **Job Properties:**
1. **Customer name**
2. **Custom 2** (which stores the cycle date)
3. **Time submitted**
4. **Workflow**

[rep_o_scen_ReprintDocument.pdf, Page 1]

#### **Document Properties:**
1. **Verification recipient**
2. **Account number**
3. **Postal code**

[rep_o_scen_ReprintDocument.pdf, Page 1]

Additionally, the **Store history records** property is set to **Yes**, so that production history (job state information) is also saved — allowing the bank to confirm that statements were printed when the original job was processed [rep_o_scen_ReprintDocument.pdf, Page 1].

---

### How These Properties Are Configured (Step-by-Step)

When configuring the StoreInRepository step, the administrator:

1. Right-clicks the **StoreInRepository** step and selects **Properties**, then clicks **Repository**.
2. Selects the target **repository** in the Repository property.
3. Selects the desired **job properties** from the *Available job properties to store* list.
4. Selects the desired **document properties** from the *Available document properties to store* list.
5. Optionally creates an **override properties file** to preserve job property values for resubmission scenarios.
6. Clicks **OK**.

## How the Printer Determines Which Color Mapping Table to Use

When a job does not have a color mapping table explicitly assigned to it, the printer falls back to its own configured default. Here is how the two-level system works:

---

### Two-Level Color Mapping Table Assignment

**Level 1 – Job Level:**
You can specify the color mapping table for an individual job by setting the **Color mapping table job property** to the file name of the desired color mapping table. [aiw02cmtjob.pdf, Page 1]

**Level 2 – Printer Level (Fallback):**
If a job does **not** have a value set for the Color mapping table job property, the printer uses the color mapping table defined in its own **Color mapping table printer property**. [aiw02cmtjob.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Scenario | Color Mapping Table Used |
|---|---|
| Job **has** a Color mapping table job property set | The table specified at the **job level** |
| Job **does not have** a Color mapping table job property set | The table specified at the **printer level** |

In other words, the **printer-level Color mapping table property acts as the default**, ensuring that jobs without an explicit assignment still receive the correct color mapping treatment. [aiw02cmtjob.pdf, Page 1]

## Order of Markup Application in RICOH ProcessDirector

When RICOH ProcessDirector applies markup to a PDF file, the **BuildPDFFromDocuments** step applies all markup elements in the following specific order:

1. **Hidden areas** *(applied first)*
2. **Images**
3. **Text**
4. **OMR marks**
5. **Barcodes** *(applied last)*

[pdfw_over_plugin_markup.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Point Regarding Hidden Areas

Hidden areas are always applied **first**, before any other markup elements. This is confirmed explicitly: *"When RICOH ProcessDirector applies markup to a PDF file, the BuildPDFFromDocuments step applies all hidden areas before applying other markup."* [pdfw_t_plugin_hidearea.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Practical Implication

This ordering is intentional and supports common workflows. For example, if you want to replace an existing optical mark with a new, smaller barcode, you can:

1. Draw a **hidden area** (cover block) over the old mark — this is applied first, blocking any ink in that region [pdfw_t_plugin_hidearea.pdf, Page 1]
2. Place a **new barcode** on top of the hidden area — this is applied last, printing the new content cleanly on top [pdfw_over_plugin_markup.pdf, Page 1]

## Removing Remaining Page Groups in RICOH Visual Workbench AFP Indexer

When you delete all trigger definitions from the control file but page groups still appear in the left pane, this means those page groups are **defined in the AFP file itself** — not in the control file. Here is how to handle this situation:

---

### Why This Happens

> *"If you delete the last trigger defined in the control file, any page groups that are defined in the AFP file itself are displayed in the left pane."*

[deletingtriggers.pdf, Page 1]

Since you can only delete trigger definitions that exist in the control file, these AFP-file-embedded page groups cannot be removed via the **Modify and Delete Definitions** window. [deletingtriggers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Remove Them

You have **two options**:

#### Option 1 — Create a New Page-Group Trigger or Fixed-Length Page Groups
Creating a new page-group trigger **or** creating fixed-length page groups will **automatically remove** any page groups defined in the AFP file itself. [deletingtriggers.pdf, Page 1]

#### Option 2 — Use Existing Page Groups (for nested page groups)
If the remaining page groups are **nested** page groups defined in the AFP file, follow these steps:

1. In RICOH Visual Workbench, click **Tools**.
2. Select **Other Page Groups**.
3. Click **Use Existing Page Groups**.

This will remove the nested page groups defined in the AFP file. [deletingtriggers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Important Caution

Be careful when making these changes if you have already created index tags or other definitions (such as barcodes created with AFP Editor) that are based on the existing page groups, as they may become invalid. [deletingtriggers.pdf, Page 1]

## Manual Edits to EnhanceAFP Control File — Will They Be Lost?

**Yes, your manual edits will be lost if you simply re-export without re-applying them.** Here is a detailed explanation of what happens and what you must do:

---

### Why Your Manual Edits Are Lost

When you manually edit an EnhanceAFP control file (for example, to add a text orientation of 90, 180, or 270 degrees), those edits are **not saved back into the Visual Workbench control file**. [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 2]

This means that if you later make additional enhancements in Visual Workbench and save them, the Visual Workbench control file has **no knowledge** of your manual edits. [vwb_CreateBarCodes.pdf, Page 3]

---

### What You Must Do to Preserve Your Manual Edits

Follow these steps each time you make new enhancements after a manual edit:

1. **Make your additional enhancements** in RICOH Visual Workbench and **save** the Visual Workbench control file. [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 2]

2. **Export a new EnhanceAFP control file** (via Tools ⇒ Export EnhanceAFP Control File) to make the new enhancements available to the workflow. [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 2]

3. **Manually re-edit the newly exported EnhanceAFP control file** to re-add all the manual edits (such as the orientation line) that you had previously added to the original EnhanceAFP control file. [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 2] [vwb_CreateBarCodes.pdf, Page 3]

---

### Example: Re-adding Text Orientation

After re-exporting, you would need to re-add a line such as the following using a text editor:

```
#Afp.InsertText.Orientation[text_name]=Degrees90
```

where `text_name` is the name identifying your text insertion. [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 2]

---

## Entering Y Position When AFP File is Rotated 90 Degrees

When defining white space in a rotated AFP file, you should enter the Y position based on the **original unrotated orientation**, not the rotated view.

Specifically, if you rotated the AFP file using the **Rotate by 90** option on the View menu, you must specify the Y position from the **top-left corner of the logical page in the unrotated view** [creatingwsdefavail.pdf, Page 1].

---

| Parameter | Reference Point |
|-----------|----------------|
| **X position** | From the top-left corner of the logical page in the **unrotated view** [creatingwsdefavail.pdf, Page 1] |
| **Y position** | From the top-left corner of the logical page in the **unrotated view** [barcode_position_tab.pdf, Page 2] |
| **Width & Height** | Measured in the **unrotated view** [barcode_position_tab.pdf, Page 2] |

---

### Important Reminder:
Even though the viewer displays the page rotated 90 degrees for your convenience, **all position and size values must always be entered as if the page were in its original, unrotated orientation** [modfiyinghiddenareas.pdf, Page 1].

This applies consistently across white space definitions, barcode areas, and hidden areas within RICOH Visual Workbench / AFP Editor.

Answer:

## Advantage of Defining a Data Object as a Resource

When a data object appears multiple times in a print job, defining it as a **resource** rather than placing it directly in a page offers a significant efficiency advantage:

> **Resources are downloaded to the printer just once and referenced as needed.**

This means that instead of sending the same data object repeatedly every time it appears in the print job, the printer receives it a single time and simply references it whenever required throughout the job.

[cac_DataObjectResources.pdf, Page 1] [cac_AFPColorPrintAndMgmt.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Comparison

| Approach | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Placed directly in a page** | The data object must be included each time it appears |
| **Defined as a resource** | Downloaded to the printer **once**, then referenced as needed — more efficient |

---

### Additional Benefit

If data objects are installed in a **resource library** (rather than included inline), you gain the further advantage of being able to **associate color conversion CMRs** with them, enabling consistent color management across print jobs. [cac_DataObjectResources.pdf, Page 1]

Additionally, storing resources centrally means you do not need to include them in every print job, and all configured print servers can access them from a shared location. [cac_CMRs.pdf, Page 1]

**No, RICOH ProcessDirector does NOT need to be installed on every computer that accesses it.** Here is how the system is structured:

## First Two Steps for Child Workflow When Splitting PDF Jobs by Size Using CreateJobsFromDocuments

When splitting PDF jobs by size using **CreateJobsFromDocuments**, the child workflow should begin with steps based on these two step templates:

---

### Step 1: **SetJobPropsFromTextFile**

This step **sets values for job properties from the steps of the child workflow**. It reads property values from a text file and applies them to the child job's properties. [pdfw_i_c_create_jt_splitsize.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: **SetJobPropsFromOriginal**

This step **copies the values that were set in the original (parent) workflow to become the values for those properties in the child workflow**. This ensures the child job inherits the appropriate property values established during parent job processing. [pdfw_i_c_create_jt_splitsize.pdf, Page 1]

|-------|--------------|--------------|
| 1st | `SetJobPropsFromTextFile` | Sets job property values from the child workflow's steps |
| 2nd | `SetJobPropsFromOriginal` | Copies property values from the original/parent workflow into the child workflow |

## One-Time Transmission: "Since Last Successful Transmission" — Will Data Be Resent?

**No, the data will NOT be sent again in the next scheduled run.**

When you perform a manual one-time transmission using the **"since the last successful transmission"** option in a REST Transmitter, the system treats it identically to a regular scheduled transmission. This means the next scheduled run will **not** include that data again.

Here is the specific explanation from the documentation:

> *"If you send all data since the last successful transmission, the transmission is treated the same as a scheduled transmission. The next scheduled transmission does not include data sent in this type of one-time transmission."*
> [reportsPostgresql_datatransObj.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Important Contrast: Specific Time Period Option

If instead you had chosen to send data for a **specific time period** (rather than "since the last successful transmission"), the behavior is **different** — that data **might** be included again in the next scheduled transmission, because it is treated as an exception:

> *"However, if you send the data for a specific time period, the transmission is treated as an exception. In the next scheduled transmission, the data might be included."*
> [reportsPostgresql_datatransObj.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| One-Time Transmission Option | Treated As | Resent in Next Scheduled Run? |
|---|---|---|
| Since last successful transmission | Scheduled transmission | ❌ No |
| Specific time period | Exception | ⚠️ Possibly Yes |

## Two Step Templates for XML Processing in RICOH ProcessDirector

RICOH ProcessDirector provides **two step templates** that manipulate XML files [aiw_o_xml_JobsWith.pdf, Page 1]:

---

### 1. 📄 `CreateJobsFromXML`

This step template **creates jobs from elements in an XML file that match an XPath expression**. The step then submits those jobs to a workflow [aiw_o_xml_JobsWith.pdf, Page 1].

**Key capabilities:**
- Reads an XML file and identifies elements matching a specified XPath expression [aiw_c_xml_PrepToReceive.pdf, Page 1]
- Creates one or more jobs based on those matching elements and submits them to a designated workflow [aiw_c_xml_PrepToReceive.pdf, Page 1]
- Can be used **multiple times** across chained workflows — for example, a first `CreateJobsFromXML` step can create a job per order, and a second can create child jobs per item within each order [aiw_c_xml_PrepToReceive.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. 🔄 `ApplyXSLTransform`

This step template **transforms XML into another format**. Specifically, it can [aiw_o_xml_JobsWith.pdf, Page 1]:
- Transform XML into a file that **specifies the values of RICOH ProcessDirector job or document properties**
- Transform XML into **another XML format**

**Additional use case:**
- If an XML element specifies a URL to download a file, `ApplyXSLTransform` can assign that URL to a job property value, which can then be used by a step based on the `DownloadFile` step template to retrieve the file [aiw_o_xml_JobsWith.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Step Template | Primary Function |
|---|---|
| `CreateJobsFromXML` | Creates jobs from XML elements matching an XPath expression and submits them to a workflow |
| `ApplyXSLTransform` | Transforms XML into job/document property files or into another XML format |

## RICOH ProcessDirector: Behavior When No Existing Media Object Matches SNMP/JMF Data

### What Happens When No Match Is Found

When a printer reports media loaded in its trays via SNMP or JMF, RICOH ProcessDirector compares that information against existing media objects. If **none of the existing media objects match**, RICOH ProcessDirector automatically **creates a new media object** with the specified values, and uses that new media object's name as the value of the **Media ready** property for the input tray [aiw_media_detection.pdf, Page 1].

More specifically, the system creates a media object of the **correct type** (either system media or printer media) with the values reported by the printer, and includes that media name in the value of the **Media ready** property [aiw_o_mediamatching.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Does the "Media to Use" Property Affect What Gets Created?

**Yes, directly.** The **Media to use** property on the printer object determines the *type* of media object that is created:

| Media to Use Setting | Comparison Target | Type of Object Created if No Match |
|---|---|---|
| **Printer** | Existing **printer media** objects | A new **printer media** object |
| **System** | Existing **system media** objects | A new **system media** object |

[aiw_media_detection.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_o_mediamatching.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Summary of the Process

1. The printer sends media tray information to RICOH ProcessDirector via **SNMP or JMF** [aiw_media_detection.pdf, Page 1].
2. RICOH ProcessDirector checks the **Media to use** property on the printer object [aiw_o_mediamatching.pdf, Page 1].
3. Based on that setting, it compares the reported media information against either **existing printer media** or **existing system media** objects [aiw_o_mediamatching.pdf, Page 1].
4. **If a match is found:** The name of the matching media object is used as the value of the **Media ready** property for that input tray [aiw_media_detection.pdf, Page 1].
5. **If no match is found:** RICOH ProcessDirector **automatically creates** a new media object of the appropriate type (printer or system) with the reported values, and uses its name in the **Media ready** property [aiw_media_detection.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_o_mediamatching.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Important Additional Notes

- If RICOH ProcessDirector does **not receive all the information** specified in the Media Matching settings (e.g., the printer only returns size but not color and weight), you will need to **manually update the created media object** to add the missing information [aiw00ccrautoms.pdf, Page 1].
- For **Ricoh PDF printers**, media information is requested via **JMF** (up to three media lists: standard, catalog, and loaded media). If a loaded media list is not returned via JMF, RICOH ProcessDirector falls back to **SNMP** [aiw00ccrautoms.pdf, Page 1].
- When the printer's media list updates (e.g., new media is loaded), **any changes made to media objects in RICOH ProcessDirector may be overwritten** by the most recent information from the printer [aiw00ccrautoms.pdf, Page 1].

## AFP Viewer: Default Page Segment Extension Search Order

According to the AFP viewer configuration file (`/opt/infoprint/ippd/afpviewer/a2pxopts.cfg` on Linux, or `C:\Program Files\Ricoh\afpviewer\a2pxopts.cfg` on Windows), the default setting for page segment extensions is as follows [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]:

```
PageSegExt=*.,*.psg,*.PSG
```

The AFP viewer searches for page segment files in this **exact order**:

| Order | Extension | Meaning |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| 1st | `*.` | No file extension |
| 2nd | `*.psg` | Lowercase `.psg` extension |
| 3rd | `*.PSG` | Uppercase `.PSG` extension |

### How the search works:
1. The viewer first checks whether the job contains an **inline resource**. If so, it uses that. [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]
2. If no inline resource is found, it looks for a file matching the resource name **with no extension** (`*.`). [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]
3. If still not found, it tries appending **`.psg`** to the filename. [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]
4. If still not found, it tries appending **`.PSG`** to the filename. [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]

> 💡 **Tip:** You can customize this order by modifying the `PageSegExt` line in the configuration file, separating additional extensions with commas. For example: `PageSegExt=*.,*.psg,*.PSG,*.300,*.600` [aiwcAFPresext.pdf, Page 1]

## Answer

No, the preset value is **not** sent to the printer automatically when a job arrives — but the behavior depends on how the **Preset name** printer property is configured.

Here is a detailed explanation:

---

### Key Behavior for AFP Printers

The documentation provides an important note specifically about this scenario:

> *"AFP jobs can request that the printer use a specific preset. When an AFP job arrives at a printer that supports this function, the printer switches to use that preset **automatically**."*
> [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 2]

However, this automatic switching **only works under a specific condition**:

---

### Critical Condition

> *"If your printer supports this function, **do not use Preset name as a scheduling property**; leave the printer property blank."*
> [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 2]

---

## Applying Visual Workbench Definitions to Production AFP Files

After finishing your page group and index tag setup in a sample AFP file using RICOH Visual Workbench, you must **add a step to one or more workflows** to apply those definitions to production AFP files. [indexingafpfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

**Step 1: Open the Workflow**
1. Click the **Workflow** tab.
2. Click the name of the workflow you want to modify. If you prefer, right-click it and choose **Copy** to work on a copy instead. [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 2: Optionally Disable the Workflow**
- Click the switch to the left of the workflow name to disable it while editing. If you do not disable it, jobs currently using the workflow may move into error when you save. [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 3: Add the Appropriate Step**
1. In the workflow editor, click the **side panel** in the top right corner.
2. Go to **Steps** and expand the **AFP TOOLS** group.
3. Select one of the following step templates: [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]
   - **IndexAFP** – Creates page groups and index tags in AFP files.
   - **EditAFP** – Can create page groups and index tags before creating barcodes, text, and hidden areas (requires AFP Editor). [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]
   - **FillWhiteSpace** – Can create page groups, index tags, barcodes, text, and hidden areas before filling white space (requires Whitespace Manager). [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]
4. **Drag** the chosen step into the workflow editor.
5. **Connect** the step to other steps. [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 4: Position the Step Correctly**
- If using **IndexAFP**, place it **before** the `EnableRepositioning` step so you can use the *Print again* action to reprint a page group. [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]
- If using **EditAFP** or **FillWhiteSpace**, position the step: [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]
  - After a step that converts line data to AFP format (e.g., `ConvertLineDataJobIntoAFP`)
  - After a step that converts Xerox data to AFP format
  - Before the `EnableRepositioning` step
  - Before a step that transforms AFP files into another format (e.g., `TransformJobIntoPDF`)
  - Before the `PrintJobs` step

**Step 5: Configure the Step Properties**
1. Right-click the step and select **Properties**.
2. If necessary, change the **General** properties.
3. Click **AFP**.
4. In the **Visual Workbench control file** field, specify the control file that contains your page group and index tag definitions. [addingindexstep.pdf, Page 1]

---

> **Key Principle:** The step you add to the workflow references the Visual Workbench control file, which is what carries your page group and index tag definitions from the sample AFP setup into production AFP file processing. [indexingafpfiles.pdf, Page 1] [aiw00c34.pdf, Page 3]

## Document Property for Tracking Damaged Mailpieces During Manual Reconciliation

Based on the provided documentation, the document property that helps operators track down the correct document to reprint is the **Mail recipient** property (`Doc.Insert.MailRecipient`).

### How It Works

When an inserter damages a mailpiece during manual reconciliation, the operator uses the **Mail recipient** property to identify and locate the correct document. Here is how it functions:

1. **Mapping**: The customer name from each document is mapped to the `Mail recipient` document property during workflow configuration. [CustomizingDocumentProperties.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Identification**: When the inserter damages a mailpiece, the operator looks at the name visible in the **address window** of the damaged mailpiece. [CustomizingDocumentProperties.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Lookup & Reprint**: The operator then uses that name — stored in the **Mail recipient** property — to find the corresponding document in RICOH ProcessDirector and mark it for reprint. [CustomizingDocumentProperties.pdf, Page 1]

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mail recipient | `Doc.Insert.MailRecipient` | Specifies the name of the person to whom the document is mailed. Inserter operators can use this property to find documents to mark for reprint during manual reconciliation. | Character | 64 characters |

Answer:

## Splitting a Large PDF Job: Is a Document Database Required?

**No, a document database is not required** to split a large PDF job into two smaller print jobs in RICOH ProcessDirector.

As explicitly stated in the documentation:

> *"RICOH ProcessDirector supports job splitting using the document properties file. A document database is not required because the same input file is used for both the original job and the production job."*
> [pdfw_c_scen_one_many.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How the Splitting Process Works (Without a Document Database)

Instead of a document database, the process relies on a **document properties file (DPF)**. Here is how the workflow is structured:

1. **Create a workflow** (e.g., named `LargeApp`) to receive and prepare the incoming data. You can copy the `SortSplitPDF` workflow as a starting point. [pdfw_c_scen_one_many.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Define the `IdentifyPDFDocuments` step**, specifying a RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat control file. This step creates the **document properties file** containing property values for each document in the job. [pdfw_c_scen_one_many.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Define the `SplitDocuments` step** in the Assemble phase to divide the job into the specified segments (e.g., 40,000 documents each). [pdfw_c_scen_one_many.pdf, Page 1]

4. **Define the `CreateJobsFromDocuments` step**, which creates the two production (child) jobs. In this step, you also define the names of the Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat control files that add markup to the PDF file. [pdfw_c_scen_one_many.pdf, Page 1]

5. **For the child jobs**, use the `AssemblePDF` workflow or a copy of it to handle printing of each child job. [pdfw_c_scen_one_many.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Technical Note

To split a job without fragmenting any documents across two jobs, you must first **identify document boundaries** using the RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat to define page groups. The `SplitDocuments` step then uses the document properties file to determine which documents go into each child job. [pdfw_i_c_create_jt_splitsize.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Yes, You Need Separate Notification Entries for Each Group

Yes, you will need to create **separate notification entries** for each group of operators, even if they are monitoring the same printer error event.

---

### Why Separate Notifications Are Required

The system is designed so that **you can create one email notification for each combination of event and recipients**. This means that different recipient groups receiving different messages — even for the same event — each require their own dedicated notification object. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]

This is explicitly illustrated with the following example from the documentation:

> *"You can create one notification to send emails to the **first shift operators** when a printer enters an error state and **another notification** to send a slightly different email message to the **second shift operators** when the same printer event occurs."*

[not_c_ConfigEmailNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Set Up Each Notification

For **each group**, follow these steps:

1. Click the **Administration** tab. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
2. In the left pane, click **Objects ⇒ Notifications**. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
3. Click **Add ⇒ Email**. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
4. Enter a **unique name** for this notification (e.g., "Printer Error – Group A"). [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
5. In the **Recipient address** field, enter the email addresses or the name of the specific **RICOH ProcessDirector group** for that notification. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
6. In the **Subject line** and **Message** fields, enter the **group-specific message** you want that group to receive. You can use symbolic notation (e.g., `${Printer.ID}`) to insert variable information. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
7. In the **Event tab**, configure the same printer error event for both notifications. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
8. Click **OK**, then **repeat the entire process** for the second group with their tailored message. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Notification | Recipients | Message | Event |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notification 1 | Group A (e.g., First Shift) | Message tailored for Group A | Printer Error |
| Notification 2 | Group B (e.g., Second Shift) | Message tailored for Group B | Printer Error |

Each notification object independently defines its own recipients, message content, and conditions, giving you full flexibility to customize communications per group. [not_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

# Automatic Email Notifications for Printer Errors in RICOH ProcessDirector

## Short Answer

**Yes** — RICOH ProcessDirector can be configured to automatically email a supervisor when a printer enters an error state, and **yes**, those emails can include log files attached. Here is a full breakdown:

---

## 1. Overview of the Feature

RICOH ProcessDirector allows you to configure the system to send an email when specific input device, job, or printer events occur — including when a printer goes into an error state. As explicitly stated in the documentation:

> *"You can send a supervisor an email with the log attached whenever a printer goes into an error state."*

[not_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

Notification emails can also be sent **conditionally**, based on time of day, specific printers, jobs, or other properties. [not_o_featov.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 2. Prerequisites: Configure Your Email/SMTP Server

Before creating notifications, you must have an email server set up. Follow these steps:

1. Collect your SMTP server details:
   - Network IP address or fully-qualified host name
   - TCP port number (standard SMTP port is 25)
   - Security type (SSL, TLS, or none) and the associated TCP port
2. If required, create a user ID and password on your SMTP server for RICOH ProcessDirector to use.
3. In RICOH ProcessDirector:
   - Click the **Administration** tab
   - Go to **Setting ⇒ System**
   - Fill in all values in the **Email/SMTP** section

[aiw_t_configemail.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 3. Creating the Printer Error Email Notification (Step-by-Step)

1. Click the **Administration** tab.
2. In the left pane, click **Objects ⇒ Notifications**.
3. Click **Add ⇒ Email**.
4. Enter a **name** for the notification.
5. Select **Printer** as the type of object to be monitored.
6. In the **Recipient address** field, enter the supervisor's email address or the name of a RICOH ProcessDirector group (e.g., a "Supervisor" group).
7. Enter a **Subject line** (you can use symbolic notation such as `${Printer.ID}` to insert dynamic values).
8. Enter the **Message** body.
9. *(Optional)* Specify a maximum number of messages to be sent within a given time period.
10. **To include the log file:** Set the **Attach log** option to **Yes** — this will attach the printer log to the email.
11. In the **Event** tab:
    - Set the property to **Printer state** and the value to the error state you want to monitor.
12. In the **Conditions** tab *(optional)*: Add any additional conditions that must be met before the notification is sent.
13. Click **OK**.

[not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 4. Example Configuration

The documentation provides a comparable example for a job error notification that illustrates the same pattern applicable to printers:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Event type | Printer |
| Recipient address | Supervisor (group) |
| Subject line | Printer Error Alert (e.g., `${Printer.ID}`) |
| Attach log | **Yes** |
| Message | Custom message with symbolic notation |
| Event property | Printer state → Error |

[not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 5. Additional Flexibility

- You can create **multiple notifications** for the same event but with **different recipients** — for example, one for first-shift operators and another for second-shift operators. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
- Notifications can be sent to **individual email addresses or entire groups** of users defined in the system. [not_c_CreateNotif.pdf, Page 1]
- You can also test your email notifications after setup to confirm they work as expected. [not_c_ConfigEmailNotif.pdf, Page 1]

## Backup Files Created by `copyConfigurationFiles.pl` with the `-b` Flag

Based on the documentation, here is the precise information regarding the `-b` flag:

---

### 📁 What Are the Backup Files Named?

When the `-b` flag is used, the backup files are named **`replaced_file.bak`** — that is, the original filename with a `.bak` extension appended. [aiwi_copyconfigurationfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ✅ Under What Condition Does It Actually Create a Backup?

The script does **not** back up every file it encounters. It will **only** create a backup under the following specific condition:

> **The file is being replaced by a *different version* of that file.**

In other words, if the file in `/aiw/aiw1/control_files` is identical to the sample file, **no backup is created**. A backup is only made when the script is actually overwriting a file with a newer/different version. [aiwi_copyconfigurationfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 📋 Important Notes

- The `-b` flag **must be used together with the `-r` flag**, since `-r` is what enables the overwriting of existing files in the first place. The syntax shown is `[-r [-b]]`, indicating `-b` is a sub-option of `-r`. [aiwi_copyconfigurationfiles.pdf, Page 1]
- A typical use case combining both flags is:
  ```
  copyConfigurationFiles.pl -r -b -w /tmp/differencesOutputFile
  ```
  This backs up files before overwriting them with newer versions. [aiwi_copyconfigurationfiles.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Step Chain Updates and Workflows

**No, changes made to a step chain after it has been placed in a workflow will NOT automatically apply to that workflow.**

This is explicitly confirmed in two separate documents:

1. **After placing a step chain in a workflow**, any modifications you make to the original step chain are not reflected in the workflow where it was already placed:

   > *"After you create a step chain and place it in a workflow, changes made to that step chain are not applied to the step chain in the workflow."* [aiw_C_StepChain.pdf, Page 1]

2. **This applies in both directions** — changes made within the workflow don't affect the original step chain, and changes made to the step chain outside the workflow don't affect the placed instance:

   > *"Changes to the steps in the current workflow do not apply to the step chain that was dropped in. Changes made to a step chain outside of the workflow are not applied to the step chains placed in the workflows."* [aiw00o36.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why does this happen?

When you drag a step chain into a workflow, the steps are **copied** into that workflow at that point in time:

> *"When you drag a step chain into one of the processing phases of another workflow, the steps from the step chain you added are **copied** into the phase where you dropped the step chain."* [aiw00o36.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What should you do if you need to update a step chain in a workflow?

Since changes are not automatically propagated, you will need to **manually update the workflow** by either:
- Editing the steps directly within the workflow itself, or
- Removing the existing step chain instance from the workflow and **dragging in the updated step chain** again.

Answer:

## Blank Pages Inserted by "Replace with job value" — Page Count & Click Charges

Based on the documentation, here is a precise explanation of what happens:

---

### What "Replace with job value" Does

When you use either **IdentifyPDFDocuments** or **BuildPDFFromDocuments** with the **Page exceptions for sides** property set to **"Replace with job value"**, the following occurs:

1. **All Sides are processed using the Duplex job property.** All existing Sides page exceptions in the JDF are removed. [aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]

2. **A blank PDF page is physically inserted** into the output PDF file for every simplex page that appears within a duplex job. [aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Are Blank Pages Counted in Total Pages?

**Yes — explicitly.** The documentation states:

> *"The blank page is counted in the Total pages property and could result in a click charge by the printer vendor for that page."*
> [aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Contrast: "Keep values from JDF" Behavior

If instead you use the **"Keep values from JDF"** value for the same property:

- All Sides page exceptions from the JDF are preserved. [aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]
- **Blank sides are NOT included in the Total pages property.** [aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]
- This means no extra click charges would be triggered for those blank sides.

---

### Summary Table

| Setting | Blank Page Inserted in PDF? | Counted in Total Pages? | Potential Click Charge? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Replace with job value** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Keep values from JDF** | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No |

[aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommendation

If avoiding extra click charges is a concern, consider using **"Keep values from JDF"** instead of **"Replace with job value"** — provided your printer controller can handle JDF Sides page exceptions. If the controller cannot process those exceptions, then **"Replace with job value"** is necessary, but you should be aware that the inserted blank pages **will** count toward Total pages and **may** incur additional charges from your printer vendor. [aiw_o_PDFPageCounts.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## Why You Can't Copy CMR Files Directly Into the Resource Library Folder

The reason is that AFP resource libraries used for CMRs rely on a critical index file called a **Resource Access Table (RAT)**, and copying files directly bypasses the process that keeps this index up to date.

Here is a detailed explanation:

---

### How the Resource Library Works

- Resource libraries that AFP Resource Installer creates use a **Resource Access Table (RAT)** as the index of the resource library. This index is stored as a file inside the library itself. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]
- When a print server needs to locate a resource, it **first consults the RAT** to see if the resource is listed there. The print server relies entirely on the RAT — if it is incorrect or out of date, the print server **cannot find resources** in the library. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What Happens When You Copy Files Directly

- If you copy CMRs or data objects directly into the resource library folder, **the RAT is not updated**. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]
- Because the RAT has no entry for the copied file, **the print server cannot use the RAT to find those CMRs or data objects**, effectively making them invisible to the print system. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]
- This is a key difference between CMRs and other AFP resources: **you cannot copy CMRs into a resource library as you can other AFP resources**. [cac_CMRs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What You Must Do Instead

You **must always use AFP Resource Installer** to manage your resource libraries, specifically to: [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

1. **Add** CMRs and data objects to a resource library.
2. **Modify** properties of data objects and CMRs listed in the RAT.
3. **Move or replicate** CMRs or data objects to a different resource library or location.

> ⚠️ Additionally, you must **never directly edit the RAT** or any files in the resource library, and you must **never replace an existing CMR by copying a new version directly** into the folder — always use AFP Resource Installer to update the resource. [cac_ManagingResources.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Copy CMR directly into folder | RAT not updated → print server cannot find the resource ❌ |
| Use AFP Resource Installer | RAT updated correctly → print server can find the resource ✅ |

## Step Templates to Copy and Customize for Quadient Inspire Designer

The two step templates you need to copy and customize to send jobs to Quadient Inspire Designer are:

1. **ComposeAFP** – A step based on this step template uses Quadient Inspire Designer to generate a new AFP file from a WFD file and one or more raw data files. The step waits for the new file to be returned. [aiw_gmc_overview.pdf, Page 1]

2. **ComposePDF** – A step based on this step template uses Quadient Inspire Designer to generate a new PDF file from a WFD file and one or more raw data files. The step waits for the new file to be returned. [aiw_gmc_overview.pdf, Page 1]

   - Data files
   - Data modules
   - Fixed data files
   - Fixed data modules
   - Quadient JOB file
   - External command

5. Click **OK**. [aiw_gmc_configsteptemplateforprintnet.pdf, Page 1]

## Handling of Selected Files When 'Create .zip file' Is Set to No (Manual Batching)

When manually batching input files with the **'Create .zip file'** property set to **No**, the system does **not** create a single job. Instead, it creates **multiple jobs** — specifically, one **child job per selected file**, plus a **parent job** to keep them together as a group.

---

### Detailed Behavior

Here is exactly what happens:

1. **You select two or more input files** in the Input Devices portlet and click **Make Batch** [aiw00j19.pdf, Page 1].

2. Because **'Create .zip file' = No**:
   - **A child job is created for each input file you selected.**
   - **A parent job is submitted to keep the child jobs together as a group.** [aiw00j19.pdf, Page 1]

3. This is consistent with the general definition of the **Batch** batching method: when 'Create .zip file' is set to No, *"all input files are submitted as child jobs"* [aiw_sdk_batch.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Contrast: When 'Create .zip file' = Yes

For comparison, if the property were set to **Yes**, all selected files would instead be **combined into a single ZIP file and submitted as one single job** [aiw00j19.pdf, Page 1] [aiw_sdk_batch.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Summary Table

| 'Create .zip file' Setting | Result |
|---|---|
| **Yes** | All files combined into one ZIP → **1 single job** |
| **No** | Each file becomes a child job → **Multiple child jobs** under 1 parent job |

# Setting Up ProcessDirector for Inserter Processing

Based on the provided documentation, to get your print jobs ready for inserter processing in RICOH ProcessDirector, you need to set up these **three key things**:

---

## 1. 🖨️ Inserter Controller Objects

You must define inserter controller objects that represent the physical inserter controllers in your installation. These objects control how RICOH ProcessDirector communicates with the inserter controller and how it reprints documents after insertion. [DefiningInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]

The inserter controller object defines:
- The scripts/commands for **sending control files** to the inserter controller and **receiving results files** back [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]
- The **rules** for writing control files and interpreting results files [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]
- The **reprint method** for documents damaged during insertion [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 2. 📋 Rules Files (for Control Files and Results Files)

You need to create **two types of rules files**:

- **Inserter control file rules** — These tell RICOH ProcessDirector how to create the control file sent to the inserter controller before insertion begins, since the format varies by manufacturer. [SettingUpInserters.pdf, Page 1]
- **Inserter results file rules** — These tell RICOH ProcessDirector how to parse the results file returned after insertion, and how to map field values to job and document properties. [SettingUpInserters.pdf, Page 1]

---

## 3. 🔄 Transfer Scripts (for Sending and Receiving Files)

You need to configure **scripts** to handle the file transfer between RICOH ProcessDirector and the inserter controller:

- Scripts to **send** inserter control files to the inserter controller
- Scripts to **receive** inserter results files back from the inserter controller

RICOH ProcessDirector provides supplied scripts (e.g., `copy_file.sh`, `ftp_file.sh`, `scp_file.sh`, `sftp_file.sh`) that you can use for these transfers. [UsingSuppliedTransferScripts.pdf, Page 3]

---

> **Summary Table**

| # | What to Set Up | Purpose |
|---|---------------|---------|
| 1 | Inserter Controller Object | Defines communication & reprint settings |
| 2 | Rules Files | Defines control file format & results file parsing |
| 3 | Transfer Scripts | Handles file movement to/from inserter controller |

## SetDeadline: Behavior When a Referenced Timestamp Property Has Not Been Set

When configuring a **SetDeadline** step with the **Deadline date** set to **"Relative to property value"**, the selected property should already have a timestamp value at the time the SetDeadline step runs. Here is what the documentation states about what happens if it does not:

---

### What Happens If the Timestamp Hasn't Been Set Yet?

If the property you selected does **not yet have a timestamp value** when the SetDeadline step runs, **RICOH ProcessDirector will be unable to determine whether the job is on schedule to meet its deadline**.

Specifically, the documentation states:

> *"The property that you select should have a timestamp value set when the SetDeadline step runs. **Until a timestamp value is set for the property, RICOH ProcessDirector cannot tell you if a job is on schedule to make its deadline.**"*
> [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Recommendation

To avoid this situation, you should ensure that the property you reference already has its timestamp populated **before** the SetDeadline step is reached in the workflow. For example:

- If you want the deadline relative to the **current time**, use the **Current time** property, which is always available when the step runs. [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]
- Place the SetDeadline step **after** any step that would populate the timestamp property you intend to reference. [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Referenced timestamp **is set** when step runs | Deadline is calculated correctly |
| Referenced timestamp **is NOT set** when step runs | RICOH ProcessDirector **cannot determine** if the job is on schedule |

Answer:

## Behavior When Adding an Index Tag to a Supplemental Page Without a Trigger

When you add an index tag to a supplemental page that has **no trigger defined**, the following happens:

> **The index tag is applied to every page outside a page group.**

This is explicitly stated in the documentation: *"You do not need to create a trigger on a supplemental page before you create an index tag. However, if the supplemental page does not contain a trigger, the index tag is applied to every page outside a page group."* [creatingsupplpagesindex.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Points to Understand

1. **A trigger is not required** before creating an index tag on a supplemental page — you can proceed directly to creating the index tag. [creatingsupplpagesindex.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Without a trigger**, AFP Indexer has no specific identifying condition to limit which pages the index tag applies to, so it defaults to applying the index tag to **all pages that fall outside any page group**. [creatingsupplpagesindex.pdf, Page 1]

3. **With a trigger**, the supplemental page is uniquely identified by a block of text in a consistent location, which restricts the index tag to only those pages matching the trigger condition. [creatingsupplpagestrigger.pdf, Page 1] [supplpages_overview.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommendation

If you want the index tag to apply only to **specific** supplemental pages (e.g., only header pages, only trailer pages), you should first define a trigger that uniquely identifies those pages before creating the index tag. [supplpages_overview.pdf, Page 1] [creatingsupplpagestrigger.pdf, Page 1]

Answer:

## AFP Full Color Management Solution Requirements

### What is Required for Full Color Management

To implement an AFP color printing solution with **full color management**, you **must use Color Management Resources (CMRs)**. [cac_AFPColorPrintAndMgmt.pdf, Page 1]

CMRs are the foundation of color management in AFP print systems. They are AFP resources that provide all the color management information — such as **ICC profiles and halftones** — that an AFP system needs to process a print job and maintain consistent color from one device to another. [cac_AFPColorPrintAndMgmt.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommended Approach for Handling Color Images

It is recommended that you **install all your color images as data objects and associate CMRs with them**. [cac_AFPColorPrintAndMgmt.pdf, Page 1]

**Data objects** contain a single type of data (such as GIF, JPEG, and TIFF images) and can be:
- Placed **directly in a page or overlay**, or
- Defined as **resources** and included in pages or overlays. [cac_AFPColorPrintAndMgmt.pdf, Page 1]

> 💡 **Best Practice:** Using a data object **as a resource** is more efficient when that object appears more than once in a print job, because resources are downloaded to the printer **just once** and referenced as needed. [cac_AFPColorPrintAndMgmt.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Optimal Performance: Centralized Resource Management

To take full advantage of the **AFP Color Management Object Content Architecture (CMOCA)**, you can store your color and image resources in a **central resource library** and let your print system manage them. This approach optimizes performance by:

- **Creating** some color management resources automatically
- **Reducing** the number of color conversion resources created at print time by generating link color conversion CMRs in advance
- **Reducing image size** by removing embedded profiles when storing them, while still retaining the association between the image and the profile
- **Marking resources as capturable**, so they can be saved on the printer and reused without being downloaded again [cac_InfoPrintColorSolutions.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| **Mandatory** | Use of Color Management Resources (CMRs) |
| **Recommended** | Install color images as data objects with associated CMRs |
| **Best Practice** | Store CMRs and data objects in a central resource library |

Answer:

## Switching RPD Processing to a Failover Server

When moving processing to the destination (failover) server, you need to run the following command:

### Command to Run on the Destination Server

**Log in as the root user** to the server you are moving processing *to*, then run:

```
/opt/infoprint/ippd/bin/changeHostname.pl server_hostname
```

[aiw_manfailover_processing.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Argument to Pass

The argument `server_hostname` should be **the name of the server you are moving processing *from***.

- If you are switching from the **production server to the failover server**, pass the **production server's hostname**.
- If you are switching from the **failover server back to the production server**, pass the **failover server's hostname**.

[aiw_manfailover_processing.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Full Step-by-Step Summary

1. Log in as the system user (default: `aiw1`) to the server you are moving processing **from** and run `stopaiw`. *(Skip this step if that server is unavailable.)*
2. Log in as **root** to the server you are moving processing **to**.
3. Run: `/opt/infoprint/ippd/bin/changeHostname.pl <source_server_hostname>`

[aiw_manfailover_processing.pdf, Page 1]

## Notifications in RICOH ProcessDirector

### Types of Notifications Available

RICOH ProcessDirector supports **three types of notification objects** that you can configure:

---

#### 1. 📧 Email Notifications
You can configure email notifications to alert users when specific **input device, printer, or job events** occur. When creating an email notification, you can specify:
- The **event** that triggers the notification
- The **subject line and content** of the email, including variable inserts (e.g., input device name, printer name, job name)
- **Recipients**, including CC and BCC
- **Conditions** that determine when the email is sent (e.g., time of day, specific states)
- A **limit** on the number of messages received within a specified time period

[not_o_NotifObj.pdf, Page 1], [not_c_ConfigEmailNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

#### 2. 🗂️ History Record Notifications *(requires Archive feature)*
These collect timestamps for job state changes. You can specify:
- Which **job states** are monitored
- What **state changes** trigger a history record (ChangedTo, ChangedFrom, Changes)
- Records include: Step, Event type, State, Phase, Workflow, Time, and Notification object Name

[not_o_NotifObj.pdf, Page 1]

---

#### 3. 🌐 Web Service Notifications *(requires Web Services Enablement feature)*
These call a **web service** (REST or SOAP) when specific input device, job, or printer events occur.

[not_o_NotifObj.pdf, Page 1], [not_c_ConfigNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ✅ Avoiding Configuration from Scratch — Copy Function

Yes! You do **not** need to configure each notification from scratch. RICOH ProcessDirector provides a **copy function** for notification objects:

> *"You can copy a notification and use it as a template for creating another notification. Copying notifications can save you time, especially when you need to create several notifications with similar properties."*

[not_c_ConfigNotif.pdf, Page 1]

This is particularly useful when, for example, you need to create multiple notifications for the same event but targeting different recipient groups or time windows. [not_c_ConfigEmailNotif.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 💡 Quick Tip: Testing Email Notifications
After creating an email notification, you can validate it by sending a **test email**:
1. Click the **Administration** tab
2. Go to **Objects → Notifications**
3. Select the notification object
4. Click **Actions → Send test email**

Note: The test email will display **"TEST"** in the subject line and use placeholders for variable inserts. [not_c_setup_notification.pdf, Page 1]

## Adding the `-enablefdp` Argument to the Media Information Command

When setting up a **TransformToPDFWithMediaInfo** step for AFP data, here is exactly what you need to do:

---

### The Argument to Add

You must add the **`-enablefdp`** argument to the **Media information command** property. [cptoutputpdf_c_WFforPDFwithMedia.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Where Exactly It Goes

The `-enablefdp` argument must be placed **between** the input argument (`-i`) and the type argument (`-type`). [cptoutputpdf_c_WFforPDFwithMedia.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Instructions

1. Open the **TransformToPDFWithMediaInfo** step in your workflow.
2. Locate the **Media information command** property.
3. Edit the command to insert `-enablefdp` in the correct position.

The correctly edited command should look like this:

```
perl ${AIWDATA}/bin/callxform.pl -C ${getControlFileName()} \
-i ${getCurrentFile(${Job.Transform.InputStream})} \
-enablefdp \
-type xif \
-loglevel I -logdate -logtime \
-logdir ${Job.SpoolFileStem}tmp \
-logfile ${Job.ID}.xif.log \
-verbose -relaxed \
-msg.add PSI3002 \
-remove abcefhilnoprst01234
```
[cptoutputpdf_c_WFforPDFwithMedia.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Important Note

This edit is **only required for AFP data streams**. If you are retrieving media information from a **PostScript** data stream, the command works without any edits. [cptoutputpdf_c_WFforPDFwithMedia.pdf, Page 1]

## ApplyPreferences Step Configuration in EnhancePDFDocuments Workflow

Based on the evidence provided, when setting up the **ApplyPreferences** step in the **EnhancePDFDocuments** workflow, two step property values need to be configured:

---

### 1. **Preferences File**
- **Set to:** `/aiw/aiw1/preferences/EnhancePDFprefs.csv`

This is the path to the CSV preferences file that contains the customer preference data to be applied to the documents. [pref_o_scen_markup.pdf, Page 2]

---

### 2. **Property Mapping**
- **Set to:** `CustomerPreferences`

This refers to the document property mapping object that defines how the columns in the preferences file correspond to document properties in RICOH ProcessDirector. [pref_o_scen_markup.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Summary Table

| Step Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Preferences file | `/aiw/aiw1/preferences/EnhancePDFprefs.csv` |
| Property mapping | `CustomerPreferences` |

These two properties together tell the ApplyPreferences step **where to find the preferences data** and **how to map that data** to the appropriate document properties during job processing. [pref_o_scen_markup.pdf, Page 2]

## Deleting a Text String Definition in RICOH Visual Workbench AFP Editor

### Removing a Previously Created Text String Definition

Yes, you can delete a text string definition you created with AFP Editor. Here are the steps:

1. In RICOH Visual Workbench, **open the sample AFP file** and the control file that contains the definitions for text strings. [deletingtextstrings.pdf, Page 1]

### Can You Delete Text Directly from the AFP File Itself?

**No, you cannot.** As explicitly stated in the documentation:

> *"You cannot delete text in the AFP file itself (instead, you can create areas to hide text)."* [deletingtextstrings.pdf, Page 1]

This is also confirmed in the text modification documentation, which similarly states:

## Device Link CMR

Based on the provided documentation, you would use a **Device Link (DL) CMR** if you want to skip the intermediate color space conversion and go directly from the input device color space to the output device color space in one step.

### Key Details:

**Device Link CMRs** work as follows:

- They use an **ICC device link profile** to convert directly from an input color space to an output color space **without reference to** an audit-mode or instruction-mode CMR [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].
- An ICC device link profile is a special kind of ICC profile specifically designed to convert the input device color space directly to the color space of an output or display device [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].
- Unlike standard color conversion CMRs — which convert colors **to and from** the ICC Profile Connection Space (PCS) in two steps — Device Link CMRs bypass the PCS entirely [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].

### Additional Important Characteristics:

- Device Link CMRs **take precedence** over audit color conversion CMRs when referenced in the MO:DCA data stream [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].
- They specify their **own rendering intent**, which overrides any other active rendering intent [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].
- A key advantage is that they **preserve the black channel (K component)** of the input color space when converting from CMYK to CMYK [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].
- You can **create, install, and uninstall** Device Link CMRs yourself [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].

> **Note:** ICC device link profiles are **not embedded in images** [cac_CMRLink.pdf, Page 1].

## The `Include` Property When Setting Estimated Durations

The **Include** property controls whether a step's estimated duration is factored into the overall calculation of the estimated duration for the job.

### What `Include` Does

When you set the `Include` property to **Yes**, the estimated duration you have configured for that step **will be included** in the calculation of the estimated duration for the job as it moves through the workflow. [dt_c_settingestimateddurations.pdf, Page 1]

### What Happens If You Set It to `No`

If you set the `Include` property to **No**, the estimated duration for that specific step **will NOT be included** in the calculation of the estimated duration for the job. [dt_c_settingestimateddurations.pdf, Page 1]

In practical terms, this means:
- The step's time will be **excluded** from the predicted completion time calculation.
- It will **not contribute** to tracking metrics such as **Percent complete**, **Tracking status**, or **Predicted completion time**. [dt_o_featov.pdf, Page 2]

### Recommended Practice

The documentation recommends setting `Include` to **Yes** for all steps you want to track, up through the last time-sensitive step in your workflow (e.g., `PrintJobs`). Steps that follow the last time-sensitive step — such as `RetainCompletedJobs` — should generally **not** have estimated durations set (or would effectively be excluded from tracking). ## Formatting and Placing the Override Properties File for StoreInRepository

When configuring the **StoreInRepository** step to preserve job property values for resubmission, follow these steps:

---

### Step 1: Create the Override Properties File

Use a text editor to create the file. [rep_c_CreateAFPWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: Format the File

Follow these formatting rules:

- **Place the database name of each job property on a separate line.** [rep_c_CreateAFPWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]
- **To add a comment**, place it on a separate line that **starts with a pound sign (`#`).** [rep_c_CreateAFPWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

**Example file contents** with three job properties (Customer name, Media required, and Duplex) and a comment: [rep_c_CreateWorkflowForJobsAndHistory.pdf, Page 1]

```
Job.CustomerName
Job.MediaRequired
# This is a comment.
Job.Duplex
```

---

### Step 3: Save and Place the File

Name the file, save it, and move it to a directory on the **RICOH ProcessDirector primary computer**. [rep_c_CreateAFPWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

Recommended locations are:

| Platform | Example Path |
|----------|-------------|
| **Linux** | `/aiw/aiw1/control_files/job_properties.txt` |
| **Windows** | `C:\aiw\aiw1\control_files\job_properties.txt` |

[rep_c_CreatePDFWorkflow.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 4: Reference the File in the StoreInRepository Step

On the **StoreInRepository** step, enter the full path and name of the file in the **"Path to override properties file"** property. [rep_c_CreateWorkflowForJobsAndHistory.pdf, Page 1]

---

> **Summary:** The override properties file is a plain text file with one job database property name per line (e.g., `Job.MediaRequired`), with optional comment lines prefixed by `#`. It can be stored in any accessible directory on the primary computer, with `/aiw/aiw1/control_files/` being the recommended location.

## Why `CreateJobsFromDocuments` is Preferred Over `CreateAFPJobsFromDocuments`

Based on the provided documentation, here is the explanation:

---

### The Recommended Approach: `CreateJobsFromDocuments`

When splitting AFP jobs into child jobs by document property, the **recommended** workflow uses `CreateJobsFromDocuments` in the parent workflow. This approach requires an additional **Assemble phase in the child workflow**, specifically a `BuildAFPFromDocuments` step, which reconstructs the AFP data for each child job from the document records. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

The recommended parent workflow includes:
- `UseInlineFormDefinition` → `IndexAFP` → `EnableRepositioning` → `IdentifyDocuments` → `GroupDocuments` → **`CreateJobsFromDocuments`**

And the child workflow includes an **Assemble phase** with `BuildAFPFromDocuments`. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1]

---

### The Alternative: `CreateAFPJobsFromDocuments`

The **alternate** workflow uses `CreateAFPJobsFromDocuments` in the parent workflow instead. [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 2]

The key difference is visible in the child workflow structure:

| Approach | Child Assemble Phase |
|---|---|
| `CreateJobsFromDocuments` | Includes `BuildAFPFromDocuments` |
| `CreateAFPJobsFromDocuments` | **No Assemble phase / no `BuildAFPFromDocuments`** |

[aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 1] [aiwdoc_i_c_create_jt_splitdocprop.pdf, Page 2]

## Two Conditions Requiring Operator Intervention in Automatic Reconciliation

Even when automatic reconciliation is configured, there are **two specific conditions** that require operator intervention:

---

### Condition 1: Reprint Percentage Exceeded
When the documents to be reprinted **exceed the percentage of reprints allowed** for the job as defined in the **Maximum documents to reprint (%)** property, the system cannot handle this automatically and operator action is required. [InserterReconciliationMethods.pdf, Page 1] [InserterOverview.pdf, Page 3]

---

### Condition 2: Unreported Document Status with No Default Set
When the **inserter controller does not report a status** for one or more documents in the job, **and** the **Default insert status** property of the inserter controller is **not set**, the system cannot determine the appropriate action automatically and operator intervention is required. [InserterReconciliationMethods.pdf, Page 1] [InserterOverview.pdf, Page 3]

> | 2 | Missing status + no default | Inserter controller reports no status **AND** Default insert status is not configured |
